top_100_positive_cdc_funded_non_suppleme.transaction_description: NC'S INTEGRATED HIV SURVEILLANCE AND PREVENTION PROJECT - AFTER SEVEN YEARS OF DECLINE AND PLATEAU IN HIV RATES, NORTH CAROLINA HAS NOTED A SMALL INCREASE IN HIV CASES FROM 2015 TO 2016 AS WELL AS LARGE INCREASES IN SYPHILIS AND HEPATITIS C OVER THE PAST THREE YEARS. WHILE THE HIV INCREASE IS SMALL, ONGOING SYNDEMICS OF HIV WITH SYPHILIS AND HCV DEMONSTRATE INCREASED TRANSMISSION RISK FOR HIV. OUR DATA ALSO SHOW AN IMPROVEMENT IN ACCESS TO AND RETENTION IN MEDICAL CARE FOR HIV DUE TO PUBLIC HEALTH AND CLINICAL CARE EFFORTS; VIRAL SUPPRESSION RESULTING FROM THIS CARE WILL REDUCE TRANSMISSION.  WE BELIEVE THAT WE ARE FACING A SITUATION OF INCREASED TRANSMISSION ON A BACKGROUND OF EFFECTIVE, BUT NOT COMPLETE, ACCESS TO CARE AND TREATMENT. OUR GOALS ARE TO DECREASE TRANSMISSION BY CONTINUING TO INCREASE ACCESS TO CARE AND PREVENTION BY BUILDING ON OUR INTEGRATED SYSTEMS AND BY CREATING INNOVATIVE, DYNAMIC, AND FORWARD-LOOKING HIV PREVENTION AND CARE ACTIVITIES.  NORTH CAROLINA IS PROUD TO BE A COLLABORATIVE, INTEGRATED AGENCY; HIV, SEXUALLY TRANSMITTED DISEASE, AND HEPATITIS B AND C PROGRAMS ARE INTEGRATED FOR BOTH SURVEILLANCE AND PREVENTION. OUR HIV SURVEILLANCE, PREVENTION, AND CARE STAFF WORK TOGETHER REGULARLY. WHILE THIS INTEGRATED STRUCTURE SUPPORTS OUR CURRENT ACTIVITIES, THIS FOA ALLOWS US TO FURTHER INTEGRATE, ADDRESSING IDENTIFIED GAPS WE HAVE NOT HAD THE FUNDS TO ADDRESS, AND ALLOWS US TO DEVELOP NEW PROGRAMS FOCUSED ON SETTINGS WHERE WE CAN MOST EFFECTIVELY INTERRUPT TRANSMISSION. THESE EFFORTS WILL IMPROVE HEALTH OUTCOMES FOR PLWH IN NORTH CAROLINA BY INCREASING THE NUMBER OF PEOPLE WHO ARE AWARE OF THEIR HIV STATUS AND VIRALLY SUPPRESSED; BY USING INTEGRATED DATA TO GUIDE PROGRAM ACTIVITIES AND FUNDING TO REDUCE HEALTH DISPARITIES; AND BY INCREASING CONFIDENTIAL AND SECURE DATA SHARING TO SUPPORT INTERVENTION AND PROGRAM PLANNING WHILE MAINTAINING A HIGH LEVEL OF DATA SECURITY AND CONFIDENTIALITY.

top_100_positive_cdc_funded_non_suppleme.transaction_description: STATE OF CONNECTICUT DEPARTMENT OF PUBLIC HEALTH - PUBLIC HEALTH EMERGENCY PREPAREDNESS COOPERATIVE AGREEMENT - THE PUBLIC HEALTH AND HEALTH CARE SYSTEM PLAY A CRITICAL ROLE IN EMERGENCY PREPAREDNESS AND RESPONSE. A MAJOR STATEWIDE OR REGIONAL EMERGENCY COULD CAUSE SEVERE ILLNESS AND/OR INJURIES AND FATALITIES. TO PREPARE FOR AND RESPOND TO AN EMERGENCY OF GREAT SEVERITY AND MAGNITUDE REQUIRES RAPID RESPONSE SURVEILLANCE AND COMMUNICATIONS SYSTEMS, A TRAINED AND AVAILABLE PUBLIC AND PRIVATE HEALTH AND MEDICAL WORKFORCE, AND VOLUNTEERS TO HELP PERFORM ESSENTIAL TASKS. THE CENTERS FOR DISEASE CONTROL AND PREVENTION (CDC) PUBLIC HEALTH EMERGENCY PREPAREDNESS (PHEP) GRANT FUNDS WILL SUPPORT ACTIVITIES THAT FURTHER DEVELOP THE PUBLIC HEALTH EMERGENCY PREPAREDNESS SYSTEMS, CAPABILITIES AND CAPACITY OF THE CT DPH AND CRI JURISDICTIONS TO ENSURE WE ARE PREPARED AND POSITIONED TO RESPOND TO AND PROTECT OUR POPULATION FROM BOTH EMERGING AND IDENTIFIED PUBLIC HEALTH RISKS AND THREATS FROM AN ALL HAZARDS APPROACH. THE CT DPH WILL WORK COLLABORATIVELY WITH GOVERNMENT, PRIVATE INDUSTRY, NON-PROFITS, AND OTHER DPH PROGRAMS TO BUILD OR SUSTAIN ITS READINESS ACROSS THE SIX PUBLIC HEALTH DOMAINS. TO MEASURE PROGRESS, THE AGENCY WILL CONTINUOUSLY EVALUATE ITS LEVEL OF PREPAREDNESS THROUGH STANDARDIZED GRANT MEASURES AND TOOLS, AS WELL AS BY EVALUATING PERFORMANCE AFTER PLANNED EXERCISES AND IN RESPONSE TO REAL EVENTS. IN ORDER TO ACHIEVE THESE GOALS, THE CT DPH MUST ENSURE THAT WE HAVE ROBUST ALL HAZARDS PUBLIC HEALTH EMERGENCY RESPONSE PLANS AND PUBLIC HEALTH CONTROL MEASURE GUIDELINES IN PLACE, RESILIENT AND WELL-PREPARED PUBLIC HEALTH SYSTEMS AND PARTNERS THAT CAN OPERATE THROUGH ALL PHASES OF A PUBLIC HEALTH DISASTER OR INCIDENT, AND CONTINUITY AND ACCESS TO PUBLIC HEALTH SERVICES, REGARDLESS OF THE EVENT. OVER THE COURSE OF THE FIVE-YEAR PROJECT PERIOD, CT WILL FOCUS ITS GRANT-RELATED INVESTMENTS, ACTIVITIES AND EFFORTS ON OUTPUTS THAT RESULT IN THE FOLLOWING LONG-TERM OUTCOMES: - TIMELY IMPLEMENTATION OF PUBLIC HEALTH INTERVENTIONS AND CONTROL MEASURES - CONTINUITY OF EMERGENCY OPERATIONS DURING PUBLIC HEALTH INCIDENTS AND SURGE CONDITIONS - TIMELY AND ACCURATE COMMUNICATION OF SITUATIONAL AWARENESS AND PUBLIC HEALTH RISK INFORMATION TO STATEWIDE PARTNERS (AS APPLICABLE) ON ESTABLISHED COMMUNICATIONS PLATFORMS AND SYSTEMS - TIMELY PROCUREMENT, AND IDENTIFYING AND UTILIZING SURGE PERSONNEL TO SUPPORT MEDICAL COUNTERMEASURES DISTRIBUTION AND DISPENSING - TIMELY COORDINATION AND SUPPORT DURING RESPONSE ACTIVITIES WITH HEALTHCARE COALITIONS AND OTHER STATEWIDE PUBLIC HEALTH AND EMERGENCY MANAGEMENT PARTNERS - EARLY IDENTIFICATION AND INVESTIGATION OF PUBLIC HEALTH INCIDENTS, OR EVENTS THAT HAVE A PUBLIC HEALTH IMPACT CONNECTICUT APPRECIATES THE AVAILABILITY OF FEDERAL FUNDS TO SUSTAIN AND BUILD UPON THE STATE’S EFFORTS TO PREPARE FOR PUBLIC HEALTH EMERGENCIES AND DISASTERS. 3.5 MILLION PEOPLE TO BE SERVED

top_100_positive_cdc_funded_non_suppleme.transaction_description: PUBLIC HEALTH EMERGENCY PREPAREDNESS (PHEP) COOPERATIVE AGREEMENT - THE OKLAHOMA STATE DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH (OSDH) IS COMMITTED TO MAINTAINING AND ENHANCING READINESS IN AN EFFORT TO STRENGTHEN THE CAPABILITY OF THE PUBLIC HEALTH AND MEDICAL SYSTEM TO EFFECTIVELY PREPARE FOR AND RESPOND TO PUBLIC HEALTH THREAT AND EMERGENCIES.  SINCE 2002 OSDH HAS UTILIZED PREPAREDNESS FUNDING TO DEVELOP AN INTEGRATED EMERGENCY RESPONSE SYSTEM THAT SPANS THE LOCAL, REGIONAL AND STATE LEVEL.  THE FOUNDATION OF THIS SYSTEM IS BUILT ON JOINT PLANNING WITH PUBLIC, PRIVATE AND TRIBAL RESPONSE PARTNERS.  AVAILABLE RESOURCES ARE LEVERAGED WHENEVER POSSIBLE TO MAXIMIZE ACHIEVEMENT OF TARGET CAPABILITIES, AND A COMPREHENSIVE TRAINING AND EXERCISE PROGRAM IS MAINTAINED TO TEST AND ENHANCE EMERGENCY RESPONSE PLANS AND CAPABILITIES.  THIS 2019-2024 FUNDING OPPORTUNITY WILL PROVIDE CRITICAL RESOURCES TO FURTHER ADVANCE OKLAHOMA’S PUBLIC HEALTH EMERGENCY RESPONSE CAPABILITIES.  OKLAHOMA WILL UTILIZE THESE FUNDS TO INCREASE OR MAINTAIN ITS LEVEL OF EFFECTIVENESS IN THE AREAS OF; COMMUNITY RESILIENCE, INCIDENT MANAGEMENT, INFORMATION MANAGEMENT, COUNTERMEASURES AND MITIGATION, SURGE MANAGEMENT, AND BIOSURVEILLANCE.  EFFORTS CARRIED OUT UNDER THIS FUNDING OPPORTUNITY WILL ENHANCE READINESS DESIGNED TO SAVE LIVE DURING EMERGENCY INCIDENTS THAT EXCEED THE DAY-TO-DAY CAPACITY AND CAPABILITY OF PUBLIC HEALTH RESPONSE AGENCIES.

top_100_positive_cdc_funded_non_suppleme.prime_award_base_transaction_description: LIGHTHOUSE CENTERS OF EXCELLENCE FOR COMPREHENSIVE INTEGRATED HIV CARE AND TREATMENT SERVICES IN MALAWI UNDER THE PRESIDENT'S EMERGENCY PLAN FOR AIDS RELIEF (PEPFAR) - BACKGROUND MALAWI HAS AN ESTIMATED HIV PREVALENCE OF 7.7% IN ADULTS AND 15,000 NEW INFECTIONS PER YEAR. THE COUNTRY MADE GREAT STRIDES TOWARDS ACHIEVING THE UNAIDS 95-95-95 TARGETS THROUGH A MULTI-SECTORAL APPROACH. TO STAY ON THIS SUCCESSFUL PATH, MALAWI HIV PROGRAM MUST APPLY MORE EFFORTS IN TARGETED TESTING FOR HIGH-RISK GROUPS, LINKING THEM TO CARE, SCALE-UP DIFFERENTIATED SERVICE DELIVERY MODELS, ADEQUATE SCREENING, AND MANAGEMENT OF ADVANCED HIV DISEASE (AHD), OPTIMIZE VIRAL LOAD (VL) MANAGEMENT, AND MITIGATE THE EFFECT OF OTHER PUBLIC HEALTH THREATS ON HIV SERVICES. LIGHTHOUSE TRUST, AN INDIGENOUS MALAWIAN ORGANIZATION, IS STRATEGICALLY POSITIONED TO ADDRESS CHALLENGES IN HIV CARE THROUGH A HOLISTIC, DATA-DRIVEN, AND LOCALLY TAILORED APPROACH. OVER THE PAST DECADES, LH ESTABLISHED CENTERS OF EXCELLENCE IN HIV CARE IN MALAWI REFERRAL HOSPITALS AND NOW OPERATES FIVE COES ACROSS THE COUNTRY IN ALL MAJOR CITIES. IN ADDITION, LH PROVIDES DIRECT SERVICE DELIVERY AND TECHNICAL SUPPORT TO PROTOTYPE FACILITIES IN LILONGWE WHICH INCLUDES EIGHT GOVERNMENT FACILITIES AND TWO PRISONS. PURPOSE THE PURPOSE OF THIS PROJECT IS TO DELIVER HIGH-IMPACT HIV TESTING AND TREATMENT SERVICES TO SUSTAIN ACHIEVEMENTS, GROW THE COHORT OF PLHIV ON ART, AND REACH THE 95-95-95 TARGETS. TO ACHIEVE THIS, LH PLANS TO CONTINUE OPERATING COES AT ALL REFERRAL HOSPITALS, IN MALAWI. THE PROJECT WILL THUS SUPPORT TERTIARY-LEVEL HIV CARE, FOCUSING ON AHD, HIV-ASSOCIATED CANCERS AND NON-COMMUNICABLE DISEASES (NCDS). MALAWI HEALTH SYSTEMS FOR HIV CARE WILL BE STRENGTHENED THROUGH MENTORSHIP, DEVELOPING MODEL INTERVENTIONS AND DIRECT SERVICE DELIVERY FOR THE PROTOTYPE FACILITIES. THUS, THE MAIN STRATEGIES OF THIS PROJECT ARE TO: OPTIMIZE STATUS-NEUTRAL TESTING SERVICES WITH IDENTIFICATION OF UNDIAGNOSED PLHIV (1ST 95) AND REFERRAL OF THE UNINFECTED FOR BIOMEDICAL PREVENTIVE SERVICES. ENSURE LINKAGE TO QUALITY CARE (2ND 95) AND OPTIMAL TREATMENT, RETENTION, AND VIRAL LOAD MONITORING (3RD 95) OF PLHIV. PROVIDE PATIENT-CENTERED, HIGH-QUALITY ADVANCED HIV TREATMENT SERVICES INCLUDING DIFFERENTIATED SERVICE DELIVERY MODELS AND INTEGRATED CARE AT ALL COES. SUPPORT THE NATIONAL ART PROGRAM THROUGH IMPLEMENTATION OF MODEL INTERVENTIONS IN PROTOTYPE CLINICS AND HEALTH-SYSTEM STRENGTHENING ACTIVITIES BEYOND COE CARE. OUTCOMES THE LONG-TERM OUTCOME OF THIS PROJECT IS THE ATTAINMENT OF THE UNAIDS 95-95-95 GOALS IN THE PROPOSED PROJECT DISTRICTS FOR ALL AGES, GENDERS, AND POPULATION GROUPS AT RISK FOR HIV INFECTION. LIGHTHOUSE WILL UNSURE THAT THAT ALL HEALTH EQUITY GAPS ARE ADDRESSED, AND EVIDENCE-BASED HIV PREVENTION INTERVENTIONS ARE OFFERED TO ALL POPULATION GROUPS. LIGHTHOUSE (LH) HAS OUTLINED A SERIES OF PRIORITIES TO IMPROVE HIV CASE FINDING, TREATMENT AND PREVENTION. THESE PRIORITIES INCLUDE INCREASING THE UPTAKE AND CONTINUITY OF PREP AMONG HIGH-RISK INDIVIDUALS AND USING TARGETED TESTING STRATEGIES TO IDENTIFY MORE UNDIAGNOSED HIV-POSITIVE INDIVIDUALS, WITH A PARTICULAR EMPHASIS ON CHILDREN 0 TO 14 YEARS, MEN, AND THE YOUTH. FURTHERMORE, LH WILL INCREASE ART COHORT GROWTH, DECREASE ATTRITION AMONG NEW ART INITIATES, AND INCREASE VIRAL LOAD SUPPRESSION ACROSS ALL AGE AND SEX GROUPS THROUGH THE VARIOUS PATIENT AND PEOPLE-CENTERED APPROACHES TO HEALTH SERVICE DELIVERY. TO SUPPORT THESE EFFORTS, LH STRENGTHEN COLLABORATION THE WITH THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH, DEPARTMENT OF HIV AND AIDS AS WELL AS HOSPITAL LEADERSHIP OF THE TERTIARY HOSPITALS AND PROTOTYPE FACILITIES. LH WILL CONTINUE BUILDING CAPACITY THROUGH CLINICAL MENTORSHIP, USING THE ESTABLISHED CASE-BASED TRAINING PLATFORM (PROJECT ECHO) TO ENSURE QUALITY SERVICES ARE BEING ALWAYS OFFERED. LH WILL USE DATA-DRIVEN QUALITY IMPROVEMENT (QI) INTERVENTIONS TO REFINE THE IMPLEMENTATION OF THESE ACTIVITIES.

top_100_positive_cdc_funded_non_suppleme.prime_award_base_transaction_description: CANCER PREVENTION AND CONTROL PROGRAMS FOR STATE, TERRITORIAL AND TRIBAL ORGANIZATIONS - ILLINOIS BREAST AND CERVICAL CANCER PROGRAM THE ILLINOIS BREAST AND CERVICAL CANCER PROGRAM (IBCCP) OFFERS FREE BREAST AND CERVICAL CANCER SCREENING AND DIAGNOSTIC SERVICES, INCLUSIVE OF MAMMOGRAMS, BREAST EXAMS, PELVIC EXAMS AND PAP TESTS.  ELIGIBLE PARTICIPANTS ARE UNINSURED OR UNDERINSURED AND HAVE INCOMES AT OR BELOW 250% OF THE FEDERAL POVERTY LEVEL.  FOR BREAST CANCER SCREENINGS, THE INDIVIDUAL MUST BE BETWEEN THE AGES OF 40 AND 64; FOR CERVICAL CANCER SCREENINGS, THE INDIVIDUAL MUST BE BETWEEN THE AGES OF 21 AND 64.  YOUNGER, SYMPTOMATIC INDIVIDUALS MAY BE DETERMINED ELIGIBLE ON A CASE-BY-CASE BASIS.  TO DATE, IBCCP HAS PROVIDED APPROXIMATELY 705,000 HIGH QUALITY SCREENING SERVICES TO 216,901 CLIENTS AND HAVE REFERRED 7,225 CLIENTS TO TREATMENT IN A TIMELY MANNER, WHICH IS DEMONSTRATED BY IBCCP’S ABILITY TO SUCCESSFULLY MEET ITS CORE INDICATORS AND MDE REQUIREMENTS ANNUALLY.  IN FEDERAL PROJECT YEAR 2023 THE IBCCP PLANS TO PROVIDE 20,500 SCREENING SERVICES.  IN ADDITION TO SCREENING AND DIAGNOSTIC SERVICES, THE IBCCP WORKS WITH HEALTH SYSTEM CLINIC PARTNERS TO IMPLEMENT EVIDENCE BASED INTERVENTIONS AND LEAD AGENCIES TO DEPLOY COMMUNITY NAVIGATORS TO ASSIST WITH BARRIER REDUCTION FOR PROGRAM CLIENTS. ILLINOIS COMPREHENSIVE CANCER CONTROL PROGRAM THE OVERARCHING MISSION FOR THE ILLINOIS COMPREHENSIVE CANCER CONTROL PROGRAM IS TO REDUCE CANCER RISK; DECREASE CANCER INCIDENCE, MORBIDITY, AND MORTALITY; REDUCE CANCER DISPARITIES; AND INCREASE QUALITY OF LIFE AMONG CANCER SURVIVORS. HEALTH DISPARITIES EXIST FOR RACIAL AND ETHNIC MINORITIES, MEDICALLY UNDERSERVED AND THE RURAL POOR POPULATIONS IN ILLINOIS, WITH HIGHER RATES OF CANCER IN RURAL AND POOR COUNTIES IN ILLINOIS. THE PROPOSED PROJECT WILL ENHANCE ILLINOIS’ CURRENT MOMENTUM AROUND CANCER PREVENTION AND EARLY DETECTION, SUPPORT AN UPDATED ILLINOIS STATE CANCER PLAN, AND BUILD CAPACITY TO STRENGTHEN PARTNERSHIPS WITH MULTI-SECTOR STAKEHOLDERS THROUGH THE UTILIZATION OF COMMUNITY HEALTH WORKERS/PATIENT NAVIGATORS TO INCREASE THE LEVEL AND REACH OF CANCER PREVENTION AND CONTROL STRATEGIES TO REACH THE ENTIRE POPULATION OF ILLINOIS AND THE HEALTH DISPARITIES POPULATION. THE ICCCP WORKS IN COLLABORATION WITH THE ILLINOIS BREAST AND CERVICAL CANCER PROGRAM (IBCCP) AND THE ILLINOIS STATE CANCER REGISTRY (ISCR), ALONG WITH OUR COMMUNITY PARTNERS IN THE ILLINOIS CANCER PARTNERSHIP (ICP) COALITION, TO ADDRESS THE BURDEN OF CANCER THROUGHOUT ILLINOIS. top_100_positive_cdc_funded_non_suppleme.prime_award_base_transaction_description: INTEGRATED HIV PROGRAMS FOR HEALTH DEPARTMENTS TO SUPPORT ENDING THE HIV EPIDEMIC IN THE UNITED STATES
top_100_positive_cdc_funded_non_suppleme.transaction_description: INTEGRATED HIV PROGRAMS FOR HEALTH DEPARTMENTS TO SUPPORT ENDING THE HIV EPIDEMIC IN THE UNITED STATES - THE CALIFORNIA DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH (CDPH) OFFICE OF AIDS (OA) IS PROPOSING A SET OF STRATEGIES AND ACTIVITIES THAT ADDRESS THE FOUR PILLARS OUTLINED IN THE FEDERAL ENDING THE HIV EPIDEMIC (ETHE) IN AMERICA INITIATIVE. CDPH OA IS SUBMITTING THE GRANT ON BEHALF OF THE SIX PHASE I COUNTIES (ALAMEDA, ORANGE, RIVERSIDE, SACRAMENTO, SAN BERNARDINO, SAN DIEGO) ASSIGNED TO CDPH OA, REFERRED TO AS THE CALIFORNIA CONSORTIUM.  BETWEEN 2011 AND 2018, FOUR OF THE SIX COUNTIES SAW A REDUCTION IN NEW HIV DIAGNOSIS, RANGING FROM FIVE PERCENT LESS TO 48 PERCENT FEWER NEW DIAGNOSIS. TWO OF THE COUNTIES HAD NOTICEABLE INCREASES IN NEW DIAGNOSIS, INCREASING 25 PERCENT AND 26 PERCENT. THIS APPLICATION INCLUDES STRATEGIES AND ACTIVITIES TO ACHIEVE THE 75 PERCENT REDUCTION IN NEW DIAGNOSIS BY THE END OF 2025.  ACTIVITIES WILL BE DIRECTED TO BLACK/AFRICAN AMERICAN AND LATINX MEN WHO HAVE SEX WITH MEN (MSM), MSM UNDER THE AGE OF 30, ESPECIALLY AMONG YOUNG MSM OF COLOR, TRANSGENDER WOMEN, PEOPLE USING SUBSTANCES—ESPECIALLY METHAMPHETAMINE AND INJECTION DRUG USE, HOMELESS INDIVIDUALS, SEX WORKERS, PRE-EXPOSURE PROPHYLAXIS (PREP) ELIGIBLE MEN AND WOMEN, AND INDIVIDUALS WITHOUT HEALTH INSURANCE OR NOT UTILIZING HEALTHCARE SERVICES.  STRATEGIES INCLUDE MORE FOCUSED HIV-TESTING, INCLUDING TAKING HIV TESTING INTO HOMELESS CAMPS AND LOCATIONS WHERE HOMELESS PEOPLE SEEK SERVICES ROUTINELY, INCLUDING STD AND HCV TESTING WITH HIV SCREENING TO INCREASE LIKELIHOOD OF PEOPLE WHO INJECT DRUGS SEEKING SCREENING, DELIVERY OF PREP OR ART AT TESTING SITES, AND PROVIDING ESSENTIAL HEALTHCARE SUCH AS BLOOD PRESSURE CHECKS, DIABETES MONITORING, AND WOUND CARE ALONG WITH SCREENING. TO INCREASE RAPID ART, PROPOSED ACTIVITIES INCLUDE USE OF PEER NAVIGATORS, SAME-DAY HIV APPOINTMENTS FOR NEWLY DIAGNOSED INDIVIDUALS, INCREASED CLINICAL DETAILING, SOCIAL MEDIA PROMOTING THE BENEFITS OF SAME-DAY ART INITIATION, AND MONITORING THE TIME BETWEEN DIAGNOSIS AND CONFIRMATION THAT INDIVIDUALS ARE ON ART. TO INCREASE PREP AND PEP USAGE, ACTIVITIES TO BE INITIATED INCLUDE DISTRIBUTING PREP IN THE COMMUNITY THROUGH MOBILE HEALTHCARE, PEER DELIVERY, PROMOTION OF PREP AND PEP AVAILABILITY AT PHARMACIES, BENEFITS COUNSELORS TO ASSIST IN ENROLLMENT IN ASSISTANCE PROGRAMS, AND MARKETING ACCURATE INFORMATION ABOUT PREP, THE READY, SET, PREP RESOURCE, THE CALIFORNIA PREP ASSISTANCE PROGRAM, AND MARKETING THE PREP ASSISTANCE PROGRAM FOR PEOPLE AGE 12 AND OLDER WHEN IT IS IMPLEMENTED.  IN ADDITION, INVESTMENT IN THE INFRASTRUCTURE OF SEXUALLY TRANSMITTED DISEASE (STD) CLINICS CREATES A CRITICAL OPPORTUNITY FOR HIV PREVENTION IN CALIFORNIA.  IN CALIFORNIA IN 2018, 63 PERCENT OF MEN WHO HAVE SEX WITH MEN (MSM) WITH PRIMARY AND SECONDARY (P&S) SYPHILIS CASES WERE HIV-NEGATIVE; 4 PERCENT WERE NEWLY DIAGNOSED WITH HIV.  CDPH ESTIMATES THAT 70 PERCENT OF MSM GONORRHEA CASES IN 2018 WERE HIV-NEGATIVE, WITH 53 PERCENT OF THOSE MSM REPORTING THAT THEY WERE NOT ON PREP.  STD CLINICS DIAGNOSE A DISPROPORTIONATELY HIGH NUMBER OF THESE CASES AND REACH THOSE AT HIGHEST RISK FOR HIV ACQUISITION, AND ARE THUS A PRIORITY FOR INITIATING HIV TESTING, LINKAGE TO CARE (LTC), RE-ENGAGEMENT IN CARE, AND INITIATION OF PREP/NON-OCCUPATIONAL POST-EXPOSURE PROPHYLAXIS (NPEP).  THREE ETHE COUNTIES HAVE EXISTING STD CLINICS WHICH WILL INCORPORATE HIV PREVENTION SERVICES INTO THEIR STD CLINICS: ORANGE, SACRAMENTO & SAN DIEGO.  THIS PROPOSAL HAS A SET OF INNOVATIVE, COMPREHENSIVE STRATEGIES AND MANY ACTIVITIES THAT INVOLVE COMMUNITY PARTICIPATION IN THEIR IMPLEMENTATION, AND SUFFICIENT STAFF TO MONITOR AND EVALUATE THE WORK BEING DONE THROUGHOUT THE CALIFORNIA CONSORTIUM. OA AND THE COUNTIES ARE READY TO IMPLEMENT THE PLAN WHEN FUNDING IS AWARDED.

top_100_positive_cdc_funded_non_suppleme.transaction_description: NEVADA PUBLIC HEALTH EMERGENCY PREPAREDNESS (PHEP) PROGRAM - THIS PHEP APPLICATION FOR NEVADA IS FOR THE CONTINUED PURPOSE OF STRENGTHENING AND ENHANCING THE CAPABILITIES OF STATE, LOCAL, AND TRIBAL PUBLIC HEALTH SYSTEMS TO RESPOND EFFECTIVELY (MITIGATE THE LOSS OF LIFE AND REDUCE THE THREATS TO THE COMMUNITY’S HEALTH AND SAFETY) TO EVOLVING THREATS AND OTHER EMERGENCIES WITHIN NEVADA. THIS ANNOUNCEMENT PROVIDES CLEAR EXPECTATIONS AND PRIORITIES FOR NEVADA TO ENHANCE THE READINESS OF THE PUBLIC HEALTH SYSTEM TO SAVE LIVES DURING EMERGENCIES THAT EXCEED THE DAY-TO-DAY CAPACITY AND CAPABILITY OF THE PUBLIC HEALTH EMERGENCY RESPONSE SYSTEM. THIS APPLICATION AIMS TO PROVIDE FUNDS TO ENSURE THAT NEVADA AND OUR PHEP SUBGRANTEES FOCUS ON ACTIVITIES TO CONTINUE TOWARD MEETING THE GOALS OF THE PUBLIC HEALTH EMERGENCY PREPAREDNESS AND RESPONSE CAPABILITIES: NATIONAL STANDARDS FOR STATE, LOCAL, TRIBAL, AND TERRITORIAL PUBLIC HEALTH. ADDITIONALLY, OUR APPLICATION AIMS TO DOCUMENT PROGRESS IN ESTABLISHING OR MAINTAINING READY PUBLIC HEALTH RESPONSE SYSTEMS WITH STRONG DISEASE SURVEILLANCE, DETECTING AND REPORTING CAPABILITIES TO ENSURE THAT NEVADA AND OUR PHEP SUBGRANTEES CONTINUE TO ADVANCE THE DEVELOPMENT OF EFFECTIVE PUBLIC HEALTH EMERGENCY MANAGEMENT AND RESPONSE PROGRAMS FOR ALL-HAZARD EVENTS WHILE COORDINATING WITH OUR HEALTHCARE COALITION PARTNERS. NEVADA HAS DEVELOPED A FIVE YEAR STRATEGIC PLAN THAT INCLUDES STRATEGIES AND ACTIVITIES BASED ON THE PHEP LOGIC MODEL AND DOMAINS, AND FINDINGS FROM OUR JURISDICTIONAL RISK ASSESSMENTS, CAPABILITY PLANNING GUIDE SELF-ASSESSMENTS, AND EXERCISE AND INCIDENT AFTER-ACTION REPORTS TO INFORM OUR STRATEGIC PRIORITIES AND PREPAREDNESS INVESTMENTS. top_100_positive_cdc_funded_non_suppleme.transaction_description: PUBLIC HEALTH EMERGENCY PREPAREDNESS (PHEP) COOPERATIVE AGREEMENT - UTAH PHEP PROJECT ABSTRACT CDC-RFA-TP19-1901 THE GOAL OF THE UTAH PUBLIC HEALTH EMERGENCY PREPAREDNESS PROGRAM IS TO ASSURE A WELL-COORDINATED, EQUIPPED, TRAINED, AND TIERED SYSTEM OF RESPONSE TO PUBLIC HEALTH EMERGENCIES AND DISASTERS IN UTAH. THE UTAH PHEP IS DESIGNED TO ADDRESS ALL PHEP CAPABILITIES, CITIES READINESS, AND MEDICAL COUNTERMEASURES INITIATIVES BY WORKING IN PARTNERSHIP WITH UDOH STATE LAB, UDOH BUREAU OF EPIDEMIOLOGY, UTAH’S LOCAL HEALTH DEPARTMENTS, UTAH’S TRIBAL NATIONS, AND WITH OTHER STATE, REGION 8, AND FEDERAL PARTNERS. THROUGH THE SUPPORT OF A PROGRAM ADVISORY COMMITTEE, THE UTAH PHEP MAINTAINS CLOSE COORDINATION WITH NUMEROUS EXTERNAL PARTNERS THROUGHOUT THE STATE. THE PROGRAM IS SUPPORTED ADMINISTRATIVELY BY THE PREPAREDNESS PROGRAMS MANAGER AND PREPAREDNESS PROGRAMS SPECIALIST. TWENTY-THREE ADDITIONAL UT DOH STAFF (AND ALSO A CDC PREPAREDNESS FIELD ASSIGNEE) ARE FUNDED UNDER THE PHEP PROGRAM TO ADDRESS SPECIFIC PROGRAM CAPABILITIES AT VARYING FTE LEVELS (TOTAL FTE – 14.4, BETWEEN LAB, EPI, PREPAREDNESS). IN-KIND AND MATCHING SUPPORT IS PROVIDED BY UDOH AND LHD PARTNERS THROUGH CONTRIBUTIONS OF TIME AND EFFORT TOWARD COMPLETING PROGRAM OBJECTIVES AT THEIR RESPECTIVE AGENCIES THROUGH STATE OR LOCALLY FUNDED ACTIVITIES. EACH PARTNER HAS A SYSTEM IN PLACE TO TRACK AND REPORT MATCHING FUNDS. THIRTEEN LHDS SERVE AS HOSTING SITES FOR PHEP SUBAWARDEE EMERGENCY RESPONSE COORDINATION (ERC) TEAMS. ERC BRING TOGETHER MULTIPLE PARTNERS WITHIN LHD GEOGRAPHIC AREAS TO CONDUCT ASSESSMENT, PREPAREDNESS PLANNING, RESPONSE COORDINATION, DEVELOPMENT OF REGIONAL EQUIPMENT CACHING, AND TRAINING AND EXERCISE ACTIVITY. UTAH’S LHDS MAINTAIN THE PRIMARY RESPONSIBILITY FOR MCM DISPENSING TO OPEN AND CLOSED POD PARTNERS IN UTAH, AS SUPPORTED BY UDOH. LHDS ALSO SERVE AS HOSTING AGENCIES FOR THE DEVELOPMENT, TRAINING, AND DEPLOYMENT OF MEDICAL RESERVE CORPS UNITS. UDOH MAINTAINS A GOVERNANCE COMMITTEE COMPOSED OF UDOH AND LHD LEADERSHIP TO REVIEW AND APPROVE PROPOSED BUDGETS AND PROJECT DELIVERABLES. PHEP CONTINUES TO MAINTAIN ESSENTIAL STATE-LEVEL SERVICES TO SUPPORT RESPONSE ACROSS ALL LEVELS AND GEOGRAPHIC SCALES. PHEP SUPPORT FOR INFORMATION AND COMMUNICATION SYSTEMS INCLUDES THE UTAH NOTIFICATION AND INFORMATION SYSTEM (UTAH’S HEALTH ALERT NETWORK), UT-NEDSS INTEGRATED DISEASE SURVEILLANCE SYSTEM, SUPPORT FOR ELR, ECR, AND SYNDROMIC SURVEILLANCE DATA FEEDS, AND NUMEROUS STATE LAB ELECTRONIC SERVICES AND REPORTING TOOLS. THE PREPAREDNESS PORTION OF THE PHEP FOCUSES ON DEVELOPING COMMUNITY PARTNERSHIPS, ENSURING CONTINUITY, DEVELOPING ALL-HAZARDS PLANS, ENSURING SUPPORT FOR INCIDENT COMMAND SYSTEMS, PARTICIPATION IN INFORMATION SYSTEMS AND PUBLIC MESSAGING, ADDRESSING FACILITY MANAGEMENT, MASS CARE ISSUES, MEDICAL SURGE, VOLUNTEERS, AND COORDINATION AND OVERSIGHT OF MEDICAL COUNTERMEASURES PROGRAMS IMPLEMENTED IN LOCAL AREAS. THE BUREAU OF EPIDEMIOLOGY AND UTAH PUBLIC HEALTH LAB FOCUS ON EARLY RECOGNITION OF THREATS, AND INFORMATION SHARING, THROUGH MAINTENANCE OF LRNB AND LRNC LAB CAPACITY AND IMPROVING ESTABLISHED INFORMATION SYSTEMS. SINCE 2002, THE VARIOUS PROGRAMS AND AGENCIES THAT WORK UNDER PHEP HAVE GROWN STRONGER, AND MORE ALIGNED, TO ENSURE EXCELLENT SUPPORT FOR UTAH’S RESIDENTS AND PUBLIC HEALTH SYSTEMS TO RESPOND TO A DISASTER OR INFECTIOUS DISEASE OUTBREAK.

top_100_positive_cdc_funded_non_suppleme.transaction_description: KANSAS PHEP COOPERATIVE AGREEMENT.  KANSAS WILL CONTINUE TO DEVELOP, SUSTAIN AND DEMONSTRATE PROGRESS TOWARD ACHIEVING THE PUBLIC HEALTH PREPAREDNESS CAPABILITIES. - KANSAS DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH AND ENVIRONMENT (KDHE) IS COMMITTED TO SUSTAINING EMERGENCY PREPAREDNESS AND RESPONSE CAPABILITY AND DEMONSTRATING OPERATIONAL READINESS TO RESPOND TO PUBLIC HEALTH THREATS AND EMERGENCIES. KDHE PREPAREDNESS PROGRAM ALSO WORKS WITH THE FOLLOWING INTERNAL KDHE AREAS TO MEET THE GOALS AND REQUIREMENTS OF THE PHEP COOPERATIVE AGREEMENT: PUBLIC HEALTH LABORATORY, EPIDEMIOLOGY, LOCAL PUBLIC HEALTH PROGRAM, AND IT. IN ADDITION, WE WILL CONTINUE TO COLLABORATE WITH MANY PARTNERS ACROSS THE STATE. THE STATE OF KANSAS HAS A DECENTRALIZED PUBLIC HEALTH SYSTEM MODEL CONSISTING OF THE STATE HEALTH DEPARTMENT, THE KANSAS DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH AND ENVIRONMENT (KDHE), AND 100 LOCAL HEALTH DEPARTMENTS SERVING ALL 105 COUNTIES IN KANSAS; ALL OF WHOM WILL PARTICIPATE IN THE PHEP COOPERATIVE AGREEMENT. PHEP FUNDING IS SPLIT EQUALLY BETWEEN KDHE AND THE LOCAL ENTITIES (WHICH INCLUDES THE 100 LOCAL HEALTH DEPARTMENTS, 15 PHEP REGIONS, AND 4 TRIBES).  KANSAS HAS TWO CITIES READINESS INITIATIVES REGIONS LOCATED IN THE NORTHEAST AND SOUTHCENTRAL AREAS. OUR STRATEGIC PRIORITIES, ARE BASED ON THE PHEP REQUIREMENTS AND HOW TO BEST MOVE THE KANSAS PREPAREDNESS PROGRAM FORWARD, ARE AS FOLLOWS: 1.	ENHANCE LOCAL/COMMUNITY/COUNTY PLANNING, RESPONSE, AND RECOVERY CAPABILITIES BY THE PROVISION OF TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE AND RESOURCES. 2.	COMPLETE A STATE-WIDE JOINT EXERCISE IN SPRING 2020. USE THE AAR/IPS TO FURTHER DEVELOP PLANNING, RESPONSE, AND RECOVERY ACTIVITIES AND PLANS. 3.	DEVELOPMENT OF A STATE JURISDICTIONAL RISK ASSESSMENT (JRA) WHICH IDENTIFIES THE PUBLIC HEALTH, MEDICAL, PRE-HOSPITAL, AND BEHAVIORAL HEALTH CONCERNS FOR THE TOP FIVE HAZARDS BY BP3. 4.	THE KANSAS HEALTH AND ENVIRONMENTAL LABORATORIES WILL ADHERE TO THE LRN-B AND LRN-C REQUIREMENTS. 5.	IMPLEMENT PLANNING, TRAINING, EXERCISE EFFORTS TO MOVE ALL CAPABILITIES TO "ESTABLISHED" BY 2024. THE PHEP LOGIC MODEL WILL BE UTILIZED TO CONDUCT ACTIVITIES ASSOCIATED TO ALL 6 DOMAINS. ACTIVITIES IN ALL 15 CAPABILITIES WILL BE INCLUDED BY THE END OF THE 5-YEAR PROJECT PERIOD TO ADDRESS CURRENT AND EMERGING RISKS AND UPDATE OUR PREPAREDNESS AND RESPONSE STRATEGIES ACCORDINGLY. THE INTENDED OUTCOMES INCOME TIMELY COMMUNICATIONS OF SITUATIONAL AWARENESS AND RISK INFORMATION BY PUBLIC HEALTH PARTNERS, CONTINUITY OF EMERGENCY OPERATIONS THROUGHOUT THE SURGE OF A PUBLIC HEALTH INCIDENT, AND EARLIEST POSSIBLE IDENTIFICATION AND INVESTIGATION OF AN INCIDENT WITH PUBLIC HEALTH IMPACT. THIS APPROACH WILL RESULT IN AN INCREASED ANNUAL PROGRESS AND AN OVERALL ENHANCED RESPONSE READINESS BY THE END OF THE PROJECT PERIOD.

top_100_positive_cdc_funded_non_suppleme.prime_award_base_transaction_description: NATIONAL BREAST AND CERVICAL CANCER EARLY DETECTION PROGRAM - EVERY WOMAN COUNTS PROGRAM - CALIFORNIA IS THE MOST POPULOUS STATE IN THE NATION, THE THIRD LARGEST GEOGRAPHICALLY, AND ONE OF THE MOST DIVERSE CULTURALLY, ETHNICALLY, AND RACIALLY. THE SIZE OF CALIFORNIA, COST OF LIVING, AND ETHNIC AND LINGUISTIC DIVERSITY CREATE CHALLENGES TO ACCESSING BREAST AND/OR CERVICAL SCREENINGS AND DIAGNOSTICS, SUCH AS THE INABILITY TO AFFORD HEALTH CARE, POOR AND UNRELIABLE PUBLIC TRANSPORTATION, LIMITED AVAILABILITY OF CULTURALLY COMPETENT MEDICAL PROVIDERS, AND/OR THE LACK OF MEDICAL PROVIDERS AND SPECIALISTS IN RURAL AREAS. AS A RESULT, MANY CALIFORNIA WOMEN ARE HAVING CHALLENGES ACCESSING AND RECEIVING TIMELY SCREENINGS AND DIAGNOSTIC SERVICES. top_100_positive_cdc_funded_non_suppleme.prime_award_base_transaction_description: NATIONAL CENTER ON HEALTH, PHYSICAL ACTIVITY AND DISABILITY - THE HEALTHCARE SYSTEM AND PUBLIC HEALTH COMMUNITY ARE OFTEN UNDERPREPARED TO SUPPORT THE NEEDS OF INDIVIDUALS WITH MOBILITY LIMITATIONS (ML) AND TO INCLUDE THEM EQUITABLY IN WELLNESS PROGRAMS (E.G., EXERCISE, LEISURE, NUTRITION, STRESS MANAGEMENT) OFFERED TO THE GENERAL COMMUNITY. IN THIS FIVE-YEAR APPLICATION, THE NATIONAL CENTER ON HEALTH, PHYSICAL ACTIVITY AND DISABILITY (NCHPAD) WILL REDUCE THESE DISPARITIES BY PROVIDING AN EVIDENCE-BASED PATHWAY FROM HEALTHCARE TO WELLNESS FOR PEOPLE WITH ML. top_100_positive_cdc_funded_non_suppleme.prime_award_base_transaction_description: FLORIDA CANCER PROGRAM - THE FLORIDA DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH APPLICATION FOR CANCER PREVENTION AND CONTROL PROGRAMS FOR STATES, TERRITORIAL AND TRIBAL ORGANIZATIONS  THE FLORIDA DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH'S APPLICATION FOR THE FUNDING OPPORTUNITY ANNOUNCEMENT DP22-2202 CANCER PREVENTION AND CONTROL PROGRAMS FOR STATES, TERRITORIAL AND TRIBAL ORGANIZATIONS INSTITUTIONALIZES A PLATFORM FOR THE COORDINATION AND INTEGRATION OF LONG-STANDING CANCER CONTROL ACTIVITIES AT THE STATE AND LOCAL LEVEL. THE CONTINUATION OF COLLABORATIVE EFFORTS WILL BE FURTHER ENHANCED BY GREATER INTEGRATION AMONG THE FLORIDA CANCER PROGRAMS’ THREE COMPONENTS, THE FLORIDA BREAST AND CERVICAL EARLY DETECTION PROGRAM, THE FLORIDA COMPREHENSIVE CANCER CONTROL PROGRAM, THE FLORIDA NATIONAL PROGRAM OF CANCER REGISTRIES. PROGRAMS WILL UNDERSCORE INCREASED COORDINATION BY EMPHASIZING A STRONGER PLANNING, EVALUATION AND HEALTH EQUITY FOCUS OVER THE NEXT FIVE YEARS.  THE CENTERS FOR DISEASE CONTROL AND PREVENTION (CDC) STATED GOALS TO ELIMINATE PREVENTABLE CANCERS, ENSURE ALL PEOPLE GET THE RIGHT SCREENING AT THE RIGHT TIME FOR THE BEST OUTCOME, AND SUPPORT CANCER SURVIVORS IN A MANNER THAT ALLOWS THEM TO LIVE LONGER, HEALTHIER LIVES.  FLORIDA INTENDS TO MEET THESE GOALS BY STRENGTHENING CANCER NETWORKS ACROSS THE STATE AND SUPPORTING DATA DRIVEN, POLICY FOCUSED INITIATIVES THAT UTILIZE RECOMMENDED EVIDENCE-BASED STRATEGIES AND ADVANCE HEALTH EQUITY WITHIN THE CANCER BURDEN. A HIGHER LEVEL OF DATA DETAIL WILL BE COLLECTED AND ANALYZED TO IMPROVE POLICY, SYSTEMS, AND ENVIRONMENTAL CHANGES IN CANCER PREVENTION AND CONTROL AND INFORM LOCAL INTERVENTIONS ACCORDINGLY.  FLORIDA IS WELL POSITIONED TO RESPOND TO THIS OPPORTUNITY SINCE THE CURRENT THREE CDC FUNDED PROGRAMS FOR CANCER CONTROL ARE INTEGRATED AND ARE MANAGED COOPERATIVELY. FLORIDA HAS LONG-ESTABLISHED RELATIONSHIPS WITH PARTNER ORGANIZATIONS, EXPERIENCED STAFF IN ALL KEY PROGRAM COMPONENTS, PROVEN PROGRAM SERVICE DELIVERY PROCEDURES TO ENHANCE COMMUNITY AND CLINICAL LINKAGES, INTEGRATION OF CANCER DATA AND REGISTRY STAFF IN PLANNING AND EXECUTION OF LOCAL, REGIONAL AND STATEWIDE EFFORTS, AND CLEARLY IDENTIFIED PRIORITY GOALS FROM THE 2020 THE FLORIDA CANCER PLAN. EFFORTS ARE DEVELOPED IN COLLABORATION WITH A STATEWIDE CANCER COALITION (THE CANCER CONTROL AND RESEARCH ADVISORY COUNCIL), SEVENTEEN REGIONAL COORDINATORS WHO NETWORK WITH PROVIDERS AND COMMUNITY PARTNERS TO RECRUIT ELIGIBLE WOMEN FOR BREAST AND CERVICAL CANCER SCREENINGS, AND SIX REGIONAL CANCER CONTROL COLLABORATIVES WHO DEVELOP REGIONAL ACTION PLANS SELECTED AMONG PRIORITY OBJECTIVES AND STRATEGIES IN THE FLORIDA CANCER PLAN.  THE CANCER PREVENTION AND CONTROL PROGRAM WILL FURTHER THE CDC GOALS AND THE FLORIDA CANCER PLAN PRIORITIES FACILITATED BY AGREEMENTS WITH FLORIDA'S HEALTH COUNCILS, COUNTY HEALTH DEPARTMENTS, AND FEDERALLY QUALIFIED HEALTH CENTERS AND IN COORDINATION WITH THE STATE'S CANCER COUNCILS, NATIONAL CANCER INSTITUTE DESIGNATED CANCER CENTERS, FLORIDA CANCER CENTERS OF EXCELLENCE, COLLABORATIVES, AND PREVIOUS AND NEW HEALTH PARTNERS.

top_100_positive_cdc_funded_non_suppleme.transaction_description: 2020-2021 PUBLIC HEALTH EMERGENCY PREPAREDNESS GRANT APPLICATION - MISSISSIPPI - MISSISSIPPI STATE DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH PUBLIC HEALTH EMERGENCY PREPAREDNESS ABSTRACT THE MISSISSIPPI STATE DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH (MSDH) M1SS1ON IS TO PROMOTE AND PROTECT THE HEALTH OF THE CITIZENS OF MISSISSIPPI. THE OVERALL GOAL OF THE MSDH'S PREPAREDNESS AND RESPONSE PROGRAMS IS TO ENSURE SUSTAINED PUBLIC HEALTH AND MEDICAL READINESS FOR OUR COMMUNITIES AND OUR STATE AGAINST BIOTERRORISM, INFECTIOUS DISEASE OUTBREAKS, OTHER PUBLIC HEALTH THREATS, MEDICAL EMERGENCIES AND NATURAL DISASTERS. THE MSDH PLANS TO ENHANCE THE PREPAREDNESS AND RESPONSE CAPABILITIES BY DEVELOPING, MAINTAINING, AND UTILIZING COLLABORATIVE RELATIONSHIPS AMONG GOVERNMENT, MENTAL/BEHAVIORAL HEALTH, PRIVATE HEALTH CARE ORGANIZATIONS, COMMUNITY AND FAITH BASED ORGANIZATIONS, AND AT RISK POPULATIONS. WE WILL DEVELOP AND UTILIZE SHARED PLANS FOR RESPONDING TO AND RECOVERING FROM DISASTERS AND EMERGENCIES WITH EACH GROUP AND CONNECT WITH STATE AND LOCAL PARTNERS TO INCREASE COMMUNICATION AND COLLABORATION FOR INCLUSION OF AT­ RISK POPULATIONS PROVIDING SUBJECT MATTER EXPERTISE IN ALL-HAZARDS EMERGENCY PREPAREDNESS AND RESPONSE PLANNING. MSDH CONTINUES TO ENHANCE OUR VOLUNTEER PROGRAM BY DEVELOPING A CREDENTIALING PROCESS FOR OUT OF STATE PROFESSIONALS COMING TO ASSIST MISSISSIPPI PROFESSIONALS DURING A DISASTER. MSDH ESTABLISHES AND MAINTAINS A STANDARDIZED AND SCALABLE OPERATIONAL STRUCTURE WITH PROCESSES THAT APPROPRIATELY ENGAGES ALL CRITICAL STAKEHOLDERS AND SUPPORTS THE EXECUTION OF CORE CAPABILITIES AND INCIDENT OBJECTIVES. WITH OPEN PODS AND OVER A THIRD OF THE STATE'S POPULATION PROTECTED BY CLOSED PODS, MISSISSIPPI HAS A VERY ROBUST STRATEGIC NATIONAL STOCKPILE PROGRAM. EACH YEAR, THE MSDH HOSTS AN PHEPSAC MEETING TO DISCUSS THE COORDINATING EFFORTS OF THE MSDH WITH LOCAL, TRIBAL AND OTHER STATE AGENCIES AND INFORM ALL INVOLVED OF THEIR RESPECTIVE ROLES IN ESF 8. THESE EFFORTS ARE INTENDED TO EXPAND THE PREPAREDNESS AND RESPONSE CAPABILITIES OF ALL ESF 8 PARTNERS AND WILL IMPROVE MISSISSIPPI'S ABILITY TO PROTECT ITS CITIZENS.

IN GENERAL, DC HEALTH HEPRA WILL ACHIEVE THIS GOAL BY FOCUSING MAINLY ON BUILDING CAPACITY AND READINESS IN THE MEDICAL COUNTERMEASURES (MCM) AND MITIGATION DOMAIN; ENSURING PUBLIC HEALTH EMERGENCY PREPAREDNESS THROUGH SOUND INVESTMENTS IN RESOURCES, PERSONNEL, TRAINING AND COMMUNITY PARTNERSHIPS; EMPHASIZING AN INTEGRATED PUBLIC HEALTH EMERGENCY RESPONSE PLANNING PROCESS IN ORDER TO STRENGTHEN THE TIES LINKING ESF#8 CAPABILITIES ACROSS FOUR DISTRICT GOVERNMENT AGENCIES; AND CAPITALIZING UPON TRAINING AND EXERCISE OPPORTUNITIES TO BUILD A SOLID UNDERSTANDING OF OUR ROLES AND RESPONSIBILITIES AMONG NON-ESF 8 EMERGENCY RESPONSE PARTNERS. THROUGH COOPERATIVE AGREEMENT CDC-RFA-TP19-1901, THE DC HEALTH PHEP PROGRAM WILL COLLABORATE WITH PARTNERS IN ORDER TO ACHIEVE APPROXIMATELY 27 PLANNED ACTIVITIES WITHIN SIX PHEP DOMAIN STRATEGIES – SOME OF WHICH WILL REQUIRE A JOINT EFFORT WITH THE DEPARTMENT’S HPP PROGRAM; THAT ALIGN TO DC HEALTH DIRECTOR’S STRATEGIC PRIORITY OF IMPLEMENTING DATA DRIVEN AND OUTCOME-ORIENTED APPROACHES TO PROGRAM AND POLICY DEVELOPMENT; AND THAT WILL CONTRIBUTE TOWARDS OUR DEPARTMENT’S REACCREDITATION BY THE PUBLIC HEALTH ACCREDITATION BOARD (PHAB).

top_100_positive_cdc_funded_non_suppleme.transaction_description: COOPERATIVE AGREEMENT FOR TUBERCULOSIS ELIMINATION AND LABORATORY IN THE STATE OF CALIFORNIA - YEAR 4 - UNITING FOR UKRAINE TUBERCULOSIS PROGRAM SUPPLEMENT ROUND 3 - ALTHOUGH THE NUMBER OF TUBERCULOSIS (TB) CASES REPORTED IN CALIFORNIA HAS DECLINED BY 61% FROM THE PEAK OF THE EPIDEMIC IN 1992, CALIFORNIA CONTINUES TO REPORT THE GREATEST NUMBER OF CASES (2,093 IN 2018) AND THE GREATEST PROPORTION (23 PERCENT) OF CASES IN THE UNITED STATES (U.S.). CALIFORNIA’S 2018 TB CASE RATE OF 5.3 PER 100,000 WAS THE THIRD HIGHEST AMONG STATES, AND NEARLY TWICE THE U.S. RATE (2.8 PER 100,000).  IN ADDITION TO THE HIGH CASE BURDEN, THERE ARE AN ESTIMATED 2 MILLION PERSONS WITH LATENT TB INFECTION (LTBI) IN CALIFORNIA, THE MAJORITY OF WHOM ARE FROM COUNTRIES WITH HIGH RATES OF TB.  THE REACTIVATION OF LTBI IN RESIDENTS BORN OUTSIDE OF THE U.S. IS THE MAIN DRIVER OF TB CASES IN CALIFORNIA. IN THE NEW PROJECT PERIOD (2020-2024), THE CALIFORNIA DEPARTMENT OF PUBLIC HEALTH (CDPH) TB CONTROL BRANCH (TBCB) WILL EMPHASIZE THE IDENTIFICATION AND LOCATIONS OF CALIFORNIA’S HIGHEST RISK POPULATIONS (AND THEIR PROVIDERS), TARGET INTERVENTIONS AND SET BASELINE PERFORMANCE FOR TARGETING TESTING AND TREATMENT METRICS AMONG THESE POPULATIONS. THE SCALING UP OF TESTING FOR AND TREATMENT OF LTBI, PARTICULARLY AMONG COMMUNITY (E.G., PRIVATE) PROVIDERS, WILL BE A FOCUS. IN ADDITION, THE TBCB AND ITS PARTNERS WILL DEVELOP A REVISED TB ELIMINATION PLAN THAT PROVIDES A ROADMAP FOR THE STATE TO CONTINUE TO MAKE PROGRESS ON TB ELIMINATION.  DESPITE SIGNIFICANT SUCCESS IN CONTROLLING TB IN CALIFORNIA, LARGE DISEASE DISPARITIES REMAIN.  THE NON-U.S.-BORN POPULATION SUFFERS A TB RATE NEARLY 14 TIMES THAT OF THE U.S.-BORN POPULATION (16.2 VS 1.2 PER 100,000 IN 2018).  TB RATES AMONG RACIAL AND ETHNIC MINORITIES IN 2018 REMAINED MUCH HIGHER THAN THOSE OF WHITES.  TB TRANSMISSION AND RESULTANT OUTBREAKS CONTINUE TO OCCUR IN THE STATE. CALIFORNIA LOCAL TB PROGRAMS AND COMMUNITY PROVIDERS ALSO CONTINUE TO BE CHALLENGED BY THE COMPLEXITY OF MANAGING MULTIPLE DRUG-RESISTANT TB (MDR TB) AND OTHER COMPLEX TB CASES.  TO ADDRESS THESE CHALLENGES, THIS APPLICATION DESCRIBES HOW THE TBCB WILL CARRY OUT SIX CORE TB CONTROL AND ELIMINATION STRATEGIES.  TB PERFORMANCE MEASURES WILL ENABLE THE TBCB TO ASSESS THE SUCCESS IN ACHIEVING THE TARGETS DESCRIBED IN THE APPLICATION.  THE TBCB ACTIVITIES CONDUCTED AS PART OF THESE STRATEGIES WILL FOCUS ON: DEVELOPING AND IMPLEMENTING INITIATIVES WITH TB PREVENTION AND CONTROL PARTNERS IN BOTH THE PUBLIC AND PRIVATE SECTORS TO IMPROVE TB CASE DETECTION, DIAGNOSIS, TREATMENT AND CASE MANAGEMENT; TARGETING HIGH-RISK POPULATIONS FOR SCREENING, TESTING OF AND TREATMENT FOR LTBI (AS WELL AS TARGETING THEIR PROVIDERS FOR EDUCATION); CONDUCTING STRUCTURED PROGRAM IMPROVEMENT AND EVALUATION ACTIVITIES TO MEASURE PERFORMANCE; IMPROVING RESPONSE TO, AND PREVENTION OF, OUTBREAKS; DECREASING RACIAL AND ETHNIC TB CASE DISPARITIES AMONG CALIFORNIA’S POPULATIONS; DEVELOPING AND IMPLEMENTING TRAINING AND EDUCATION EFFORTS TO STRENGTHEN PREVENTION AND CONTROL ACTIVITIES; AND STRENGTHENING THE CAPACITY OF THE CDPH MICROBIAL DISEASES LABORATORY TO ENSURE PROMPT AND ACCURATE LABORATORY TESTING FOR MYCOBACTERIUM TUBERCULOSIS. A SPECIFIC EMPHASIS WILL BE ON DEVELOPING NEW AND STRENGTHENING CURRENT PARTNERSHIPS TO FURTHER CONTROL AND ELIMINATE TB IN CALIFORNIA.  THE CDPH TBCB IS AN ESTABLISHED TB PROGRAM WITH SUBSTANTIAL EXPERIENCE IN DEVELOPING, IMPLEMENTING AND EVALUATING TB PREVENTION AND CONTROL STRATEGIES AND ACTIVITIES. STAFF INCLUDE PHYSICIANS, NURSES, EPIDEMIOLOGISTS, HEALTH EDUCATORS AND OTHERS WHO TOGETHER CONSTITUTE A MULTI-DISCIPLINARY TEAM CAPABLE OF IMPLEMENTING THE TBCB PREVENTION AND CONTROL PLAN FOR CALIFORNIA.

top_100_positive_cdc_funded_non_suppleme.transaction_description: PUBLIC HEALTH EMERGENCY PRERAREDNESS (PHEP) - PUBLIC HEALTH PREPAREDNESS AND RESPONSE (PHPR) COOPERATIVE AGREEMENT HOSPITAL PREPAREDNESS PROGRAM (HPP) COOPERATIVE AGREEMENT 2019-2023 PROJECT PERIOD  PROJECT ABSTRACT FUNDS FOR THE HOSPITAL PREPAREDNESS PROGRAM (HPP) AND PUBLIC HEALTH EMERGENCY PREPAREDNESS (PHEP) COOPERATIVE AGREEMENTS ARE INTENDED TO IMPROVE THE JURISDICTION’S ABILITY TO WITHSTAND ADVERSITY, STRENGTHEN HEALTH AND EMERGENCY RESPONSE SYSTEMS AND ENHANCE THE STATE’S OVERALL HEALTH SECURITY, AS WELL AS TO STRENGTHEN THE CAPABILITY OF THE PUBLIC HEALTH SYSTEM TO EFFECTIVELY PREPARE FOR AND RESPOND TO PUBLIC HEALTH THREATS AND EMERGENCIES.  HPP FUNDING WILL CONTINUE FOSTERING ISLAND WIDE HEALTH CARE DELIVERY SYSTEM READINESS, TARGETING THE IMPROVEMENT OF PATIENT OUTCOMES AND CONTINUOUS EFFORTS TO ENABLE RAPID RECOVERY FROM CATASTROPHIC EVENTS THROUGH THE ONGOING DEVELOPMENT OF HCCS, THEIR PRIORITIES AND OBJECTIVES. top_100_positive_cdc_funded_non_suppleme.prime_award_base_transaction_description: CANCER PREVENTION AND CONTROL PROGRAMS - SC DOH'S OVERALL PROGRAM ABSTRACT: THE SOUTH CAROLINA CANCER PREVENTION AND CONTROL PROGRAMS SUPPORT THE NATIONAL IMPLEMENTATION OF A COMPREHENSIVE AND COORDINATED APPROACH TO INFORM POLICY, SYSTEMS, AND ENVIRONMENTAL CHANGE STRATEGIES TO PREVENT AND CONTROL CANCER, PROVIDE HIGH QUALITY BREAST AND CERVICAL CANCER SCREENING SERVICES AND WORKWITH STATEWIDE CANCER COALITIONS TO PLAN AND IMPLEMENT CANCER CONTROL PRIORITIES, AND SURVEILLANCE PROGRAMS TO MONITOR AND REPORT CANCER BURDEN. BUILDING ON THE WORK OF PROGRAMS PREVIOUSLY FUNDED UNDER DP1701WHICH SUPPORTED THE COORDINATION AND INTEGRATION OF SC DHEC’S LONG-STANDING CANCER ACTIVITIES TO REDUCE CANCER MORBIDITY AND MORTALITY, THISAPPLICATION SUPPORTS THE ACHIEVEMENT OF THE FOLLOWING CANCER PREVENTION AND CONTROL GOALS: INCREASE EARLY IDENTIFICATION OF CANCER, REDUCE LATE-STAGE DIAGNOSIS, CLOSE THE GAP ON CANCER DISPARITIES, REDUCE CANCER INCIDENCE AND MORTALITY, AND ELIMINATE PREVENTABLE CANCERS. ADDITIONALLY, SC DHEC’S CANCER PROGRAMS ENSURE ALL PEOPLE GET THE RIGHT SCREENING AT THE RIGHT TIME FOR THE BEST OUTCOME, AND SUPPORT CANCER SURVIVORS IN A MANNER WHICH ALLOWS THEM TO LIVE LONGER, HEALTHIER LIVES. SC CCCP, SC NBCCEDP AND SCCCR COLLABORATE AND COORDINATE APPROACHES THAT LEVERAGE CROSS-CUTTING PRIORITIES TO IMPLEMENT CANCER PREVENTION AND CONTROL ACTIVITIES TO REDUCE THE BURDEN OF CANCER IN SOUTH CAROLINA AND EXTENDS TOIMPLEMENTATION OF WORK THAT WILL BE COMPLETED BY CONTRACTED PARTNERSHIPS SHARED BETWEEN THE INTERNAL PROGRAMS.SCCCR WILL CONTINUE TO ENHANCE AND IMPLEMENT STRATEGIES TO COLLECT TIMELY, COMPLETE, AND ACCURATE CANCER INCIDENCE DATA ON ALL REPORTABLE INCIDENT CANCER CASES AND WORK WITH SC CCCP AND SC NBCCEDP PROGRAMS AND OTHER PARTNERS TO PROMOTE INCREASED UTILIZATION OF SCCCR DATA IN NEW AND INNOVATIVE WAYS TO ADDRESS THE CANCER BURDEN, CANCER DISPARITIES, AND TO IMPROVE CANCER OUTCOMES AND HEALTH EQUITY. THE SC CCCP AND SC NBCCCEDP WILL MONITOR AND ANALYZESCCCR DATA, OTHER SURVEILLANCE DATA, AND OTHER PERTINENT DATA SOURCE STO PRIORITIZE, PLAN, AND IMPLEMENT EVIDENCE-BASED STRATEGIES GUIDED BY HEALTH DISPARITIES, SOCIAL DETERMINANTS OF HEALTH, AND DISPROPORTIONATELY DISADVANTAGED INDIVIDUALS AND COMMUNITIES.  NEW PARTNERSHIPS AND COLLABORATIONS WILL BE TARGETED, AND EXISTING ONES ENHANCED FOR INCREASED IMPLEMENTATION OFSTRATEGICAND INNOVATIVE WAYS TO ADDRESSCANCER INCIDENCE,MORTALITY,ANDDISPARITIES,ESPECIALLY IN AREAS AND AMONG POPULATIONS AND COMMUNITIES WITH THE HIGHEST RATES.THESE INTERNAL AND EXTERNAL PARTNERSHIPS WILL ENHANCE SC DHEC’S EFFORTS TO: (1) ADMINISTER CANCER RISK REDUCTION AND PRIMARY PREVENTION PROCEDURES, (2) EXPAND EARLY DETECTION AND TREATMENT PRACTICES, (3)IMPROVE HEALTH EQUITY, (4)PROMOTE A QUALITY OF LIFE FOR CANCER PATIENTS, THEIR FAMILIES AND CARETAKERS, AND THOSE IN REMISSION, AND (5)DEVELOP AND EXECUTE SUSTAINABLE POLICY AND SYSTEMS CHANGES.

top_100_positive_cdc_funded_non_suppleme.prime_award_base_transaction_description: SUSTAINING THE CAPACITY OF PROVINCIAL HEALTH OFFICES TO COORDINATE AND PROVIDE QUALITY, COMPREHENSIVE AND SUSTAINABLE HIV/AIDS PREVENTION, CARE AND TREATMENT SERVICES IN ZAMBIA UNDER PEPFAR - THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH HAS INCLUDED HIV/AIDS AS ONE OF ITS GOALS. IT AIMS TO ACHIEVE HIV EPIDEMIC CONTROL, BY REDUCING NEW HIV INFECTIONS AND AIDS RELATED MORTALITY BY 75% (ZAMBIA NATIONAL HEALTH STRATEGIC PLAN). HIV MODELS SUGGEST THAT THE NUMBER OF NEW HIV INFECTIONS IN ZAMBIA STILL EXCEEDS THE NUMBER OF DEATHS AMONGST PLHIV. THE HIV PREVALENCE RATE AMONG WOMEN AND MEN AGED 15-49 IN ZAMBIA IS 11.1%; THE PREVALENCE IS HIGHER AMONG WOMEN THAN MEN AT 14.2% AND 7.5% RESPECTIVELY (ZDHS, 2018). ACCORDING TO ZDHS 2018, THE HIV PREVALENCE RATE FOR SOUTHERN PROVINCE IS 12.4% WHICH IS ABOVE THE NATIONAL HIV PREVALENCE RATE. SPHO IMPLEMENTS A COMBINATION OF HIV PREVENTION INTERVENTIONS, TARGETING HIV NEGATIVE MEN AND WOMEN, ADOLESCENT GIRLS AND YOUNG WOMEN (AGYW), PREGNANT AND BREASTFEEDING WOMEN (PBFW), KEY AND VULNERABLE POPULATIONS (KVPS) AS WELL AS OTHER POPULATIONS AT HIGH RISK OF HIV ACQUISITION. SPHO HAS ADOPTED A DECENTRALIZED APPROACH TO POST GBV CARE. CURRENTLY SPHO IS PROVIDING ROUTINE HIV PREVENTION, CARE AND TREATMENT SERVICES, INCLUDING TB/HIV SERVICE IN CORRECTIONAL FACILITIES IN 5 DISTRICTS. IN COP21, SPHO CONTINUED TO PROVIDE COORDINATION SUPPORT TO DREAMS AND DREAMS-LIKE IMPLEMENTING PARTNERS (IPS). SOUTHERN PROVINCE SUPPORTS HTS SERVICES IN THE SUPPORTED FACILITIES. SPHO ADOPTED MIXED METHODS FOR CASE FINDING FOR ADULTS AND CHILDREN. OPD TESTING IS ROUTINE IN ALL THE HEALTH FACILITIES WITH THE USE OF THE HIV RISK SCREENING TOOL FOR ADULTS ABOVE 15 YEARS. SPHO IMPLEMENTS HTS INDEX TESTING, SOCIAL NETWORK TESTING AND HIV SELF-TEST (HIVST). SPHO ACHIEVED 56% PMTCT STAT WITH KNOWN HIV STATUS TOWARDS THE ANNUAL TARGET OF 64, 674 IN FY22 (SAPR 2022). IN ADDITION, SPHO TESTED 1896 HEI AND IDENTIFIED 57 POSITIVES WHO ARE ON ART. SPHO WILL CONTINUE PROVIDING EMTCT SERVICES THROUGH A FAMILY CENTERED APPROACH APPROVED BY MOH. PAEDIATRIC HIV/ART PROGRAMMING IS ONE OF THE KEY PRIORITY AREAS FOR THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH HIV PROGRAM PRIMARILY BECAUSE OF LAGGING IN ATTAINING THE UNAIDS 95, 95, 95 FOR CHILDREN AND ADOLESCENTS LIVING WITH HIV. TO CLOSE THE GAP SPHO IMPLEMENTED PAEDIATRIC AND ADOLESCENT SURGE IN SELECTED FACILITIES. AT SAPR FY22 SPHO MANAGED TO ATTAIN 22% (262/1197) CASE FINDING AGAINST THE TARGET, 69 % VLC WITH 94% VLS. SPHO WILL SUPPORT 15 DISTRICTS IN THE PROVISION OF ART SERVICES AND HAVE MADE SIGNIFICANT STRIDES IN ENROLLING HIV POSITIVE CLIENTS ON TREATMENT. FURTHER, THE SPHO COLLABORATES WITH OTHER IPS WITHIN THE PROVINCE FOR EFFECTIVE TREATMENT PROGRAMING. SPHO WILL CONTINUE TO FOCUS ITS SUPPORT ON INCREASING THE NUMBER OF HIV+ PEOPLE ACCESSING ART TREATMENT, REDUCE ITT (INTERRUPTION TO TREATMENT) AND ENSURE DURABLE VIRAL LOAD SUPPRESSION IN THE 15 DISTRICTS. AT SAPR FY22, A TOTAL NUMBER OF 6171 WERE IDENTIFIED HIV POSITIVE ACROSS ALL THE SUPPORTED DISTRICTS, REPRESENTING A 49% ACHIEVEMENT OF FY22 ANNUAL TARGET OF 12,492. SPHO ACHIEVED A TX_CURR 134 000 REPRESENTING 91% TOWARDS FY 22 ANNUAL TARGET OF 148,006. TO IMPROVE VIRAL LOAD COVERAGE SPHO WILL IMPLEMENT VIRAL LOAD AND EID POINT OF CARE TESTING USING GENEXPERT. SPHO WILL SCALE UP RECENCY TESTING TO ALL THE FACILITIES. SPHO HAS BEEN IMPLEMENTING AN ACCELERATED STRATEGY FOR THE ELIMINATION OF CERVICAL CANCER BY 2030. ACCORDING TO SAPR FY 22 A TOTAL NUMBER OF 15,527 WOMEN LIVING WITH HIV (WLHIV) WERE SCREENED FOR CERVICAL CANCER REPRESENTING 50% ACHIEVEMENT TOWARDS THE ANNUAL TARGET. COVERAGE OF SCREENING SERVICES IS STILL LOW AT 13% (50/370 FACILITIES).

top_100_positive_cdc_funded_non_suppleme.transaction_description: INTEGRATED HIV SURVEILLANCE AND PREVENTION--CHICAGO - PROJECT TITLE:   		CHICAGO INTEGRATED HIV PREVENTION AND SURVEILLANCE PS18-1802 PROGRAM APPLICANT:		CHICAGO DEPARTMENT OF PUBLIC HEALTH ADDRESS:		333 S. STATE STREET, SUITE 200, CHICAGO, IL 60604 BUSINESS OFFICIAL: 	ANNE POSNER, DIRECTOR OF HEALTH EQUITY  DEMOGRAPHICS OF HIV POPULATIONS IN CHICAGO IN 2015, THERE WERE 921 NEW HIV INFECTION DIAGNOSES IN CHICAGO. AMONG NEW DIAGNOSES, 79% WERE LINKED TO CARE WITHIN 30 DAYS AND 90% BY 12 MONTHS. GROUPS MOST IMPACTED INCLUDED MEN (83% OF NEW HIV DIAGNOSES); GAY, BISEXUAL, AND OTHER MEN WHO HAVE SEX WITH MEN (MSM) (76%); NON-HISPANIC BLACKS (54%); AND INDIVIDUALS AGED 20-29 YEARS OLD (43%). NEW HIV INFECTIONS WERE CLUSTERED IN SPECIFIC COMMUNITY AREAS ON THE NORTH, SOUTH, AND WEST SIDES OF THE CITY. BETWEEN 2000 AND 2010, THE ESTIMATED ANNUAL PERCENT DECREASE IN NEW HIV DIAGNOSES WAS 6.2%, REPRESENTING A 50% REDUCTION IN THE ACTUAL NUMBER OF NEW DIAGNOSES (1850 TO 991). BETWEEN 2011 AND 2015, THE PERCENT CHANGE OF DECREASE SLOWED TO 2.8%, REPRESENTING A 7% REDUCTION IN THE ACTUAL NUMBER OF NEW DIAGNOSES (991 TO 921). OF THE 23,355 CHICAGOANS LIVING WITH HIV IN 2015, ONLY 40% WERE RETAINED IN CARE, AND 48% PERCENT WERE VIRALLY SUPPRESSED. WHILE POPULATION-LEVEL DATA ARE NOT AVAILABLE, WE ESTIMATE THAT 10% OF VULNERABLE HIV-NEGATIVE INDIVIDUALS ARE USING PRE-EXPOSURE PROPHYLAXIS (PREP).  PROGRAM OUTCOMES THROUGH OUR INTEGRATED HIV PREVENTION AND SURVEILLANCE STRATEGIES OUTLINED IN OUR PROPOSAL, OVER THE COURSE OF THIS FIVE-YEAR COOPERATIVE AGREEMENT, THE CHICAGO DEPARTMENT OF PUBLIC HEALTH (CDPH) WILL MAKE PROGRESS TOWARD ACHIEVING ITS PRIORITY OUTCOMES. BY 2022, CDPH EXPECTS TO INCREASE BY 10% THE NUMBER OF PLWH WHO ARE VIRALLY SUPPRESSED AND 10% THE NUMBER OF VULNERABLE HIV NEGATIVE INDIVIDUAL WHO USE PREP. THE HIV/STI BUREAU’S HIV SERVICES PORTFOLIO CREATES AN OPTIMAL ENVIRONMENT FOR ACHIEVING THE SHORT, INTERMEDIATE, AND LONG-TERM OUTCOMES IDENTIFIED IN THIS FUNDING OPPORTUNITY ANNOUNCEMENT. THROUGH OUR PROPOSED DEMONSTRATION PROJECT, CDPH WILL ADAPT AND IMPLEMENT A DATA SHARING TOOL (KNOWN AD HIV DATA ENCLAVE) TO IMPROVE COORDINATION WITHIN CDPH HIV/STI PROGRAMS, AND BETWEEN ILLINOIS DEPARTMENT OF PUBLIC HEALTH (IDPH) AND CDPH TO ENSURE CONTINUITY OF PREVENTION AND CARE SERVICES FOR PEOPLE WHO CROSS JURISDICTIONAL BOUNDARIES. THE HIV DATA ENCLAVE APPLICATION WILL BUILD UPON THE “BLACK BOX” CONCEPT WITH SIGNIFICANT ENHANCEMENTS AND APPLICATIONS, INCLUDING: (I) SECURE HOSTING AND AUTOMATED DATA FEEDS WITHIN HEALTH DEPARTMENT FIREWALLS; (II) A COMBINED HIV SURVEILLANCE AND HIV PROGRAM DATA CENTER TO FACILITATE CROSS-JURISDICTIONAL PREVENTION AND CARE COORDINATION; (III) AUTOMATED DATA FEEDBACK TO INITIAL DATA SOURCES TO UPDATE SURVEILLANCE DATA WITH CURRENT CLIENT INFORMATION AND CARE STATUS; AND (IV) GENERATION OF ROUTINE AUTOMATED REPORTS, LINE LISTINGS OF PEOPLE NOT IN CARE, AND EPIDEMIOLOGICAL DATA TABLES/GRAPHS TO INCREASE DATA DISSEMINATION AND PROGRAM MONITORING.

top_100_positive_cdc_funded_non_suppleme.transaction_description: INTEGRATED HIV SURVEILLANCE AND PREVENTION PROGRAMS FOR HEALTH DEPARTMENTS - THE VIRGINIA DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH (VDH), DIVISION OF DISEASE PREVENTION (DDP) WILL UTILIZE FUNDING UNDER CDC-RFA-PS18-1802 TO IMPLEMENT A COMPREHENSIVE AND INTEGRATED HIV SURVEILLANCE AND PREVENTION PROGRAM THAT WILL: 1) PREVENT NEW INFECTIONS; 2) IMPROVE HEALTH OUTCOMES FOR PERSONS LIVING WITH HIV (PLWH); AND 3) REDUCE RELATED HEALTH DISPARITIES.  DDP WILL WORK TO IMPROVE COMPLETENESS AND TIMELINESS OF HIV SURVEILLANCE DATA AND INCREASE THE USE OF INTERVENTIONAL SURVEILLANCE. DDP WILL EXPAND DATA TO CARE ACTIVITIES, UTILIZE DDP’S CARE MARKERS DATABASE AND OTHER DATA SOURCES TO GENERATE OUT-OF-CARE (OOC) LISTS TO FACILITATE LINKAGE AND RE-ENGAGEMENT OF PLWH INTO HIV CARE; AND DISTRIBUTE OOC LISTS EVERY SIX MONTHS TO LINKAGE STAFF AT AGENCIES WHERE THE CLIENT LAST RECEIVED HIV-RELATED SERVICES. DDP WILL ENGAGE IN DATA SYSTEM UPGRADES AND AUTOMATION OF SURVEILLANCE PROCESSES TO REDUCE MANUAL DATA ENTRY, WORK CLOSELY WITH ALL HIV CARE FACILITIES TO MOVE TO ELECTRONIC LABORATORY REPORTING, AND IMPROVE SYSTEM AND PROCESS EFFICIENCY AND INTEGRATION BETWEEN HIV SURVEILLANCE, PREVENTION, AND CARE PROGRAMS.  DDP WILL INCREASE THE NUMBER OF PEOPLE WHO RECEIVE AN HIV TEST AND LEARN THEIR STATUS; INCREASE THE PERCENTAGE OF HIV-NEGATIVE PERSONS REFERRED TO AND LINKED TO HIV PRE-EXPOSURE PROPHYLAXIS AND NON-OCCUPATIONAL POST-EXPOSURE PROPHYLAXIS; SUPPORT PROVISION OF PARTNER SERVICES; INCREASE THE PERCENTAGE OF NEWLY DIAGNOSED AND OOC PLWH SUCCESSFULLY LINKED TO CARE; PROMOTE CONTINUITY OF SERVICES FOR PLWH INCLUDING RETENTION AND ADHERENCE INTERVENTIONS, SOCIAL AND SUPPORT SERVICES, AND BEHAVIORAL INTERVENTIONS; DISTRIBUTE CONDOMS; INITIATE SYRINGE SERVICES; AND PROVIDE PRIORITY POPULATIONS WITH BEHAVIORAL INTERVENTIONS, COMMUNITY–LEVEL AND SOCIAL MARKETING INTERVENTIONS, STIGMA REDUCTION, AND SERVICE NAVIGATION.   PRIORITY POPULATIONS WILL INCLUDE PLWH AND THEIR SEXUAL AND INJECTION PARTNERS; GAY AND BISEXUAL MEN AND OTHER MEN WHO HAVE SEX WITH MEN; PERSONS WHO INJECT DRUGS; TRANSGENDER PERSONS; AND HIGH-RISK HETEROSEXUALS. EMPHASIS WILL BE PLACED ON REACHING BLACKS AND LATINOS WHO ARE DISPROPORTIONATELY IMPACTED BY HIV IN VIRGINIA. DDP WILL WORK COLLABORATIVELY WITH LOCAL HEALTH DISTRICTS, COMMUNITY-BASED ORGANIZATIONS (CBOS), MEDICAL PROVIDERS, CORRECTIONAL FACILITIES, FAITH INSTITUTIONS, AND UNIVERSITIES.  DDP WILL CONTINUE TO PROVIDE AND/OR COORDINATE CAPACITY BUILDING ASSISTANCE (CBA) ACTIVITIES FOR CBOS, MEDICAL PROVIDERS, AND VDH STAFF THROUGH USE OF THE CBA REQUEST INFORMATION SYSTEM, VIRGINIA HIV/AIDS RESOURCE AND CONSULTATION CENTERS, MID-ATLANTIC AIDS EDUCATION AND TRAINING CENTERS, LOCAL CBA PROVIDERS, QUARTERLY CONTRACTOR MEETINGS, AND DIRECT PROVISION OF TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE BY DDP STAFF.  THE HIV SURVEILLANCE, CARE, AND PREVENTION UNITS WILL COLLABORATE ON PLANNING, MONITORING, AND EVALUATION TO ASSESS PROGRESS IN MEETING THE GOALS OF THE VIRGINIA INTEGRATED SERVICES PLAN AND DEVELOP A NEW PLAN BY THE END OF THE FUNDING CYCLE.   COMPONENT B: DEMONSTRATION PROJECT VDH WILL IMPLEMENT A DATA-TO-CARE RX (D2C-RX) INTERVENTION FOR CLIENTS SERVED THROUGH THE VIRGINIA AIDS DRUG ASSISTANCE PROGRAM USING REAL-TIME PHARMACY CLAIMS DATA TO IDENTIFY CLIENTS WHO MISS PICKING UP HIV MEDICATIONS AT 30, 60, AND 90-DAY INTERVALS. VDH WILL EXPAND D2C EFFORTS WHICH ARE CURRENTLY FOCUSED ON CLIENTS WHO ARE "OUT OF CARE" TO TARGET THOSE WHO ARE AT RISK TO FALLING OUT OF CARE BY IDENTIFYING CLIENTS WHO MAY NOT BE PICKING UP MEDICATIONS IN A TIMELY MANNER. VDH WILL EXPAND AND ADAPT EXISTING PROTOCOLS, CONSENTS, AND DATA SYSTEMS TO DEVELOP, IMPLEMENT, AND EVALUATE THIS PROJECT.  THIS DEMONSTRATION PROJECT WILL AIM TO IMPROVE HEALTH OUTCOMES OF RETENTION IN CARE AND VIRAL SUPPRESSION ALONG THE HIV CARE CONTINUUM, MORE HOLISTICALLY INTEGRATE REAL-TIME DATA USED TO MONITOR THESE OUTCOMES, AND IDENTIFY PROGRAM PLANNING OPPORTUNITIES TO SUPPORT CONTINUOUS ENGAGEMENT IN CARE FOR ALL PLWH IN VIRGINIA.

top_100_positive_cdc_funded_non_suppleme.prime_award_base_transaction_description: WASHINGTON STATE CANCER PREVENTION AND CONTROL PROGRAMS - THE WASHINGTON STATE DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH (DOH) IS APPLYING FOR FUNDING FOR THREE PROGRAMS UNDER CDC’S DP22-2202, CANCER PREVENTION AND CONTROL PROGRAMS FOR STATE, TERRITORIAL, AND TRIBAL ORGANIZATIONS.  DOH’S BREAST, CERVICAL AND COLORECTAL HEALTH PROGRAM (BCCHP), COMPREHENSIVE CANCER CONTROL PROGRAM (CCCP), AND THE WA STATE CANCER REGISTRY (WSCR) PROPOSE A COLLABORATIVE APPROACH TO ELIMINATE CANCER DISPARITIES IN WASHINGTON.  BCCHP WILL IMPROVE HEALTH EQUITY BY INCREASING COMMUNITY-DRIVEN PARTNERSHIPS, INCREASING THE UTILIZATION OF QUALITY CANCER SURVEILLANCE AND DATA, PROVIDING SCREENING, OUTREACH, AND NAVIGATION FOR THOSE POPULATIONS DISPROPORTIONATELY AFFECTED BY BREAST AND CERVICAL CANCER, AND INCREASING UTILIZATION OF SUSTAINABLE EVIDENCE-BASED INTERVENTIONS TO INCREASE CANCER SCREENING RATES.  CCCP WILL ENHANCE THE UTILIZATION OF CANCER REGISTRY DATA TO INFORM IMPLEMENTATION EFFORTS AND THE UPDATE OF THE WA STATE PLAN FOR HEALTHY COMMUNITIES. THE PROGRAM INTENDS TO INCREASE ACCESS TO SELF-MANAGEMENT PROGRAMS AND INCREASE SOCIAL, PHYSICAL AND ECONOMIC SUPPORT THAT PROMOTE HEALTHY LIFESTYLE BEHAVIORS THAT REDUCE CANCER RISK, PROMOTE SCREENING AND SUPPORT THE WELLNESS OF CANCER SURVIVORS THROUGH A VARIETY OF COLLABORATIVE INITIATIVES. OUR CANCER REGISTRY PROGRAM, WSCR, WILL STRIVE TO INCREASE CAPACITY, FLEXIBILITY AND UTILITY OF WSCR INFRASTRUCTURE TO MEET THE EVER CHANGING CANCER REGISTRY NEEDS AND STANDARDS. FASTER REPORTING OF HIGH QUALITY DATA WILL SUPPORT OUR RESEARCHERS IN IMPROVING TREATMENT AND FINDING A CURE. OUR COLLABORATIVE APPROACH WITH THE THREE PROGRAMS AND OUR STATEWIDE STAKEHOLDERS WILL CREATE A WASHINGTON WITH LESS CANCER AND ADVANCE HEALTH EQUITY FOR WASHINGTONIANS.

top_20_records_by_obligation.transaction_description: JUNE 2023 SUPPLEMENTAL FUNDING PROGRAMS: HHS BRIDGE ACCESS AND VACCINE CONFIDENCE - THE VISION OF THE TEXAS DEPARTMENT OF STATE HEALTH SERVICES (DSHS) IMMUNIZATION PROGRAM (PROGRAM) IS A TEXAS FREE OF VACCINE-PREVENTABLE DISEASES. THE MISSION OF THE TEXAS DSHS IMMUNIZATION PROGRAM IS TO REMOVE BARRIERS TO COMPLETE AND TIMELY VACCINATION, INCREASE VACCINE COVERAGE LEVELS, AND REDUCE THE BURDEN OF VACCINE-PREVENTABLE DISEASES FOR ALL TEXAS INFANTS, CHILDREN, ADOLESCENTS, AND ADULTS. THE PROGRAM SEEKS TO PREVENT, REDUCE AND ULTIMATELY ELIMINATE VACCINE-PREVENTABLE DISEASES WITH AN EMPHASIS ON IMPROVING IMMUNIZATION COVERAGE AMONG OUR YOUNGEST CITIZENS, CHILDREN UNDER THREE YEARS OF AGE. MAJOR ACTIVITIES ARE ORGANIZED AROUND ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS, SUCH AS ASSESSING IMMUNIZATION COVERAGE; DISEASE SURVEILLANCE AND OUTBREAK RESPONSE; EDUCATING HEALTHCARE PROFESSIONALS; PROVIDING NEEDED INFORMATION TO PARENTS, SCHOOLS AND THE PUBLIC; REDUCING BARRIERS TO VACCINE ACCESS THROUGH THE TEXAS VACCINES FOR CHILDREN PROGRAM; ASSURING ADEQUATE VACCINE SUPPLY; MONITORING AND SUPPORTING PROVIDERS TO ENSURE PROPER VACCINE HANDLING AND ACCOUNTING; AND OPERATING IMMTRAC2, THE STATEWIDE IMMUNIZATION REGISTRY. THE PROGRAM ALSO SEEKS TO PROMOTE ADOLESCENT AND ADULT VACCINATIONS. ADOLESCENT IMMUNIZATION RATES ON HPV, TDAP, AND MCV ARE COMMUNICATED TO SITES ENROLLED IN THE TVFC PROGRAM DURING SITE REVIEWS. EDUCATION ON ACTIVITIES TO INCORPORATE AT THE SITE TO RAISE ADOLESCENT RATES, SUCH AS REMINDER/RECALL AND SIMULTANEOUS ADMINISTRATION IS PROVIDED TO STAFF DURING THE REVIEW. IN ADDITION, DSHS COMMUNICATES THE TDAP/HPV RATIO (1TDAP:2HPV) TO ALL ENROLLED SITES TWICE ANNUALLY. THIS COMMUNICATION CONTAINS INFORMATION ON ACTIVITIES TO INCORPORATE TO RAISE ADOLESCENT RATES.  THE PROGRAM EDUCATES PROVIDERS ON THE ACIP REQUIREMENTS AND IMMUNIZATIONS STANDARDS FOR ADOLESCENTS AND ADULTS. IN ADDITION, DSHS OPERATES AN ADULT SAFETY NET (ASN) PROGRAM THAT OFFERS MOST ACIP-RECOMMENDED VACCINES TO UNINSURED ADULTS IN FEDERALLY QUALIFIED HEALTH CENTERS, RURAL HEALTH CLINICS, DSHS AND LOCAL HEALTH DEPARTMENT CLINICS. IN ADDITION, OTHER SITES THAT PARTICIPATE IN THE ASN PROGRAM INCLUDE HIV/STD CLINICS AND DRUG TREATMENT FACILITIES. ANNUALLY, DSHS STAFF CONDUCT A SITE REVIEW AT FACILITIES THAT ARE ENROLLED ONLY IN ASN TO REVIEW STORAGE AND HANDLING PRACTICES, ELIGIBILITY PRACTICES AND ALL OTHER POLICIES AND PROCEDURES REQUIRED OF THE PROGRAM. IMMUNIZATION SERVICE DELIVERY IN TEXAS IS COMPLICATED BY A NUMBER OF FACTORS. TEXAS SHARES A LARGE INTERNATIONAL BORDER WITH MEXICO, AND MANY HEALTH PROBLEMS FACED BY MEXICO MUST BE ADDRESSED IN THE ADJACENT AREAS. THE PROGRAM MUST MEET THE NEEDS OF BOTH LARGE, URBAN CENTERS AND SPARSELY-POPULATED RURAL AREAS. THE DIVISION OF TEXAS INTO 254 COUNTIES UNDER LOCAL JURISDICTION MAKES STANDARDIZATION DIFFICULT. NO SINGLE INTERVENTION STRATEGY ALONE IS SUCCESSFUL IN INCREASING IMMUNIZATION COVERAGE LEVELS. A COMBINATION OF BEST PRACTICES, IMPLEMENTED CONSISTENTLY, CAN HELP TO RAISE IMMUNIZATION LEVELS. THE PROGRAM HAS IDENTIFIED AND PROMOTES THE FOLLOWING BEST PRACTICES: REMINDER AND RECALL SYSTEMS, THE MEDICAL HOME, REGISTRIES AND ROBUST EDUCATION FOR BOTH PROVIDERS AND THE PUBLIC. PARTNERSHIPS ARE AN IMPORTANT TOOL IN PUTTING THESE BEST PRACTICES INTO ACTION.  RAISING IMMUNIZATION LEVELS IS A COLLABORATIVE EFFORT THAT BENEFITS FROM THE COMMITMENT OF OTHER PROGRAMS AND AGENCIES SUCH AS TEXAS HEALTH AND HUMAN SERVICES; AND THE TEXAS EDUCATION AGENCY, AS WELL AS PRIVATE SECTOR PARTNERS SUCH AS THE TEXAS MEDICAL ASSOCIATION, TEXAS PEDIATRIC SOCIETY, AND THE TEXAS PHARMACY ASSOCIATION. THE PROGRAM WILL CONTINUE TO WORK WITH PARTNERS TO REACH OUT TO THEIR CONSTITUENCIES AND ENHANCE THEIR IMMUNIZATION EFFORTS. FUNDING OF THIS APPLICATION WILL MAKE IT POSSIBLE FOR THE PROGRAM TO CONTINUE SUPPORT OF IMMUNIZATION ACTIVITIES ON A STATEWIDE BASIS.

top_20_records_by_obligation.prime_award_base_transaction_description: PARTNERING WITH NATIONAL ORGANIZATIONS TO SUPPORT COMMUNITY-BASED ORGANIZATIONS TO INCREASE VACCINATION COVERAGE ACROSS DIFFERENT RACIAL AND ETHNIC ADULT POPULATIONS CURRENTLY EXPERIENCING DISPARITIES - THE CDC FOUNDATION WILL SUPPORT EFFORTS TO INCREASE ACCESS AND ACCEPTANCE OF INFLUENZA AND COVID-19 VACCINES AMONG ADULTS IN RACIAL AND/OR ETHNIC POPULATIONS EXPERIENCING DISPARITIES IN THE UNITED STATES. THE CDC FOUNDATION WILL USE THREE MAIN STRATEGIES TO ACHIEVE THIS GOAL: 1) FUND COMMUNITY-BASED ORGANIZATIONS (CBOS) TO ENGAGE AND BUILD TRUST WITH TARGET COMMUNITIES, 2) BUILD THE CAPACITY OF CBOS TO IMPLEMENT AND EVALUATE SUCCESSFUL COMMUNITY INTERVENTIONS WITH A HEALTH EQUITY FOCUS, AND 3) SUPPORT EFFECTIVE PARTNERSHIPS AND THE DISSEMINATION OF TOOLS, RESOURCES AND BEST-PRACTICES THROUGH THE CREATION OF A RESOURCE HUB.BY BUILDING THE CAPACITY AND RESILIENCY OF CBOS THROUGH PARTNERSHIPS AND RESOURCE SHARING, THE CDC FOUNDATION WILL EXPAND THE IMPLEMENTATION OF EVIDENCE-BASED INTERVENTIONS TO ADDRESS VACCINE MISINFORMATION, EXPAND VACCINE OPPORTUNITIES AND INCREASE VACCINE COVERAGE. THE CDC FOUNDATION WILL OVERSEE THE DESIGN, DEVELOPMENT, AND MANAGEMENT OF A SEARCHABLE REPOSITORY PLATFORM TO HOUSE A MULTI-LINGUAL INVENTORY OF COMMUNICATION MATERIALS AND TOOLS TO SUPPORT COLLABORATIVE EFFORTS TO INCREASE ADULT IMMUNIZATION. THE CDC FOUNDATION WILL FACILITATE CBO NETWORKING, PROVIDE LINKAGES TO TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE AND SUBJECT MATTER EXPERTS, AND BUILD THE CAPACITY OF CBOS.  THE CDC FOUNDATION FULLY EMBRACES CDC?S STRATEGY TO ADDRESS DISPARITIES IN INFLUENZA AND COVID-19 VACCINATION RATES BASED ON RACE AND ETHNICITY. BY THE END OF THE PROJECT, CBOS WILL HAVE INCREASED CAPABILITIES AND ACCESS TO COMMUNICATION MATERIALS TO BETTER ADDRESS VACCINE HESITANCY AND HEALTH INEQUITIES AMONG BLACK, INDIGENOUS AND PEOPLE OF COLOR (BIPOC) COMMUNITIES. AN EXPECTED PROJECT OUTCOME IS TO STRENGTHEN AUTHENTIC, COMMUNITY DIALOGUE THROUGH CBO ENGAGEMENT ACTIVITIES THAT ADDRESS VACCINE MISINFORMATION AND SUPPORT INDIVIDUALS IN OPENLY WEIGHING AVAILABLE OPTIONS, RISKS, AND BENEFITS ? AT BOTH A PERSONAL AND A COMMUNITY LEVEL, ALONG WITH HOW THEIR LIVED EXPERIENCE FAC TORS INTO THESE DECISIONS. THIS PROJECT WILL SIGNIFICANTLY INCREASE THE NUMBER OF CBOS ENGAGED IN PUBLIC HEALTH AND VACCINE EDUCATION AND DELIVERY. ANOTHER IMPORTANT OUTCOME WILL BE AN INCREASE IN THE KNOWLEDGE, ENGAGEMENT, VACCINE CONFIDENCE AND ACCEPTANCE RATES IN TARGET BIPOC COMMUNITIES. THE PROJECT WILL ASSESS THE DIFFERENT CBO STRATEGIES, ACTIVITIES, AND RESULTS TO PROVIDE FINDINGS AND RECOMMENDATIONS FOR INCREASING VACCINE ACCEPTANCE AMONG AT-RISK POPULATIONS.

THE PROGRAM ALSO SEEKS TO PROMOTE ADOLESCENT AND ADULT VACCINATIONS. ADOLESCENT IMMUNIZATION RATES ON HPV, TDAP, AND MCV ARE COMMUNICATED TO SITES ENROLLED IN THE TVFC PROGRAM DURING SITE REVIEWS. EDUCATION ON ACTIVITIES TO INCORPORATE AT THE SITE TO RAISE ADOLESCENT RATES, SUCH AS REMINDER/RECALL AND SIMULTANEOUS ADMINISTRATION IS PROVIDED TO STAFF DURING THE REVIEW. IN ADDITION, DSHS COMMUNICATES THE TDAP/HPV RATIO (1TDAP:2HPV) TO ALL ENROLLED SITES TWICE ANNUALLY. THIS COMMUNICATION CONTAINS INFORMATION ON ACTIVITIES TO INCORPORATE TO RAISE ADOLESCENT RATES.  THE PROGRAM EDUCATES PROVIDERS ON THE ACIP REQUIREMENTS AND IMMUNIZATIONS STANDARDS FOR ADOLESCENTS AND ADULTS. IN ADDITION, DSHS OPERATES AN ADULT SAFETY NET (ASN) PROGRAM THAT OFFERS MOST ACIP-RECOMMENDED VACCINES TO UNINSURED ADULTS IN FEDERALLY QUALIFIED HEALTH CENTERS, RURAL HEALTH CLINICS, DSHS AND LOCAL HEALTH DEPARTMENT CLINICS. IN ADDITION, OTHER SITES THAT PARTICIPATE IN THE ASN PROGRAM INCLUDE HIV/STD CLINICS AND DRUG TREATMENT FACILITIES. ANNUALLY, DSHS STAFF CONDUCT A SITE REVIEW AT FACILITIES THAT ARE ENROLLED ONLY IN ASN TO REVIEW STORAGE AND HANDLING PRACTICES, ELIGIBILITY PRACTICES AND ALL OTHER POLICIES AND PROCEDURES REQUIRED OF THE PROGRAM. IMMUNIZATION SERVICE DELIVERY IN TEXAS IS COMPLICATED BY A NUMBER OF FACTORS. TEXAS SHARES A LARGE INTERNATIONAL BORDER WITH MEXICO, AND MANY HEALTH PROBLEMS FACED BY MEXICO MUST BE ADDRESSED IN THE ADJACENT AREAS. THE PROGRAM MUST MEET THE NEEDS OF BOTH LARGE, URBAN CENTERS AND SPARSELY-POPULATED RURAL AREAS. THE DIVISION OF TEXAS INTO 254 COUNTIES UNDER LOCAL JURISDICTION MAKES STANDARDIZATION DIFFICULT. NO SINGLE INTERVENTION STRATEGY ALONE IS SUCCESSFUL IN INCREASING IMMUNIZATION COVERAGE LEVELS. A COMBINATION OF BEST PRACTICES, IMPLEMENTED CONSISTENTLY, CAN HELP TO RAISE IMMUNIZATION LEVELS. THE PROGRAM HAS IDENTIFIED AND PROMOTES THE FOLLOWING BEST PRACTICES: REMINDER AND RECALL SYSTEMS, THE MEDICAL HOME, REGISTRIES AND ROBUST EDUCATION FOR BOTH PROVIDERS AND THE PUBLIC. PARTNERSHIPS ARE AN IMPORTANT TOOL IN PUTTING THESE BEST PRACTICES INTO ACTION.  RAISING IMMUNIZATION LEVELS IS A COLLABORATIVE EFFORT THAT BENEFITS FROM THE COMMITMENT OF OTHER PROGRAMS AND AGENCIES SUCH AS TEXAS HEALTH AND HUMAN SERVICES; AND THE TEXAS EDUCATION AGENCY, AS WELL AS PRIVATE SECTOR PARTNERS SUCH AS THE TEXAS MEDICAL ASSOCIATION, TEXAS PEDIATRIC SOCIETY, AND THE TEXAS PHARMACY ASSOCIATION. THE PROGRAM WILL CONTINUE TO WORK WITH PARTNERS TO REACH OUT TO THEIR CONSTITUENCIES AND ENHANCE THEIR IMMUNIZATION EFFORTS. FUNDING OF THIS APPLICATION WILL MAKE IT POSSIBLE FOR THE PROGRAM TO CONTINUE SUPPORT OF IMMUNIZATION ACTIVITIES ON A STATEWIDE BASIS.

top_20_records_by_obligation.transaction_description: CDC-RFA-IP19-1901 IMMUNIZATION AND VACCINES FOR CHILDREN - THE GEORGIA DEPARTMENT OF PUBLIC HEALTH, IMMUNIZATION PROGRAM (GIP) PROVIDES A WIDE ARRAY OF CRITICAL PREVENTION SERVICES FOR GEORGIANS WHO ARE AT RISK OF ACQUIRING VACCINE PREVENTABLE DISEASES.  THE GIP SEEKS TO LOWER THE INCIDENCE AND RISK OF VACCINE PREVENTABLE DISEASE BY PROVIDING VACCINE, MONITORING IMMUNIZATION RATES, AND PROVIDING EDUCATION AND TRAINING PROGRAMS FOR PUBLIC AND PRIVATE IMMUNIZATION PROVIDERS STATEWIDE. THE GIP ENSURES THAT THE GEORGIA POPULATION IS PROTECTED FROM VACCINE PREVENTABLE DISEASES THROUGH VARIOUS PROGRAMS, INCLUDING; THE VACCINES FOR CHILDREN (VFC) PROGRAM WHICH PROVIDES PUBLIC PURCHASED VACCINE, FOR ELIGIBLE CHILDREN, AT NO CHARGE TO VFC ENROLLED PROVIDERS, THE ADULT VACCINE PROGRAM (AVP) WHICH PROVIDES PUBLIC PURCHASED VACCINE, FOR ELIGIBLE ADULTS, AT NO CHARGE TO AVP ENROLLED PROVIDERS, THE GEORGIA REGISTRY OF IMMUNIZATION TRANSACTIONS AND SERVICES (GRITS) COLLECTS AND MAINTAINS ACCURATE AND CURRENT VACCINATION RECORDS TO PROMOTE DISEASE PREVENTION AND CONTROL, THE EDUCATION AND TRAINING PROGRAM ENSURES IMMUNIZATION PROGRAM STAFF RECEIVE TRAINING ON IMMUNIZATION AND VACCINE PREVENTABLE DISEASE IN ORDER TO PROVIDE EDUCATION FOR HEALTH CARE PROVIDERS AND CONSUMERS, THE SPECIAL POPULATIONS PROGRAM TARGETS ADOLESCENTS AND ADULTS AND STRIVES TO INCREASE COVERAGE RATES IN THESE POPULATIONS, THE FIELD SERVICES AND ASSESSMENT PROGRAM PROVIDES A QUALITY IMPROVEMENT STRATEGY, INCLUDING ANNUAL ASSESSMENTS OF SCHOOL AND CHILDCARE IMMUNIZATION STATUS, TO RAISE IMMUNIZATION COVERAGE LEVELS AND IMPROVE STANDARDS OF PRACTICE AT THE PROVIDER LEVEL, VACCINE PREVENTABLE DISEASE (VPD) SURVEILLANCE PROGRAM TRACKS AND MONITORS VPD CASES AND OUTBREAKS AND PROVIDES CASE MANAGEMENT FOR CASES AND THEIR CONTACTS, THE GEORGIA IMMUNIZATION STUDY PROGRAM COLLECTS AND ANALYZES IMMUNIZATION COVERAGE DATA FOR OUR TWO YEAR OLD AND 7TH GRADE POPULATIONS, PUBLISHING THE DATA IN A WRITTEN FORMAT ANNUALLY, AND THE PERINATAL HEPATITIS B PREVENTION PROGRAM TRACKS INFANTS BORN TO HEPATITIS B-INFECTED MOTHERS TO ENSURE THEIR INFANTS COMPLETE THE HEPATITIS B VACCINE SERIES AND POST-VACCINATION TESTING. GIP GOALS CONTINUE TO INCLUDE A FOCUS ON INCREASING IMMUNIZATION RATES IN ALL POPULATIONS, ANNUALLY INCREASING PROVIDER USE OF GRITS, EDUCATING PROVIDERS AND STAFF ON KEY IMMUNIZATION TOPICS IN ORDER TO PROTECT THEMSELVES, THEIR FAMILIES, AND THE COMMUNITY FROM VACCINE PREVENTABLE DISEASES, INCREASING COLLABORATION WITH OUR COUNTERPARTS IN ORDER INCREASE ENROLLMENT IN THE VFC AND AVP PROGRAMS AND REACH TARGET POPULATIONS AND GROUPS AT GREATEST RISK OF BEING UNDER-IMMUNIZED.  ADDITIONALLY, THE GIP WILL CONTINUE TO ENHANCE STEWARDSHIP AND ACCOUNTABILITY FOR ALL PUBLICLY PURCHASED VACCINE AND VFC, 317, PPHF, AND PAN FLU GRANT FUNDING, ASSESS PROGRAM PERFORMANCE FOR PROGRAM IMPROVEMENT, ASSURE ACCESS TO VACCINES, ASSURE THAT THE IMMUNIZATION INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY INFRASTRUCTURE SUPPORTS PROGRAM GOALS AND OBJECTIVES, AND IMPROVE AND MAINTAIN PREPAREDNESS. THE GIP WILL ACHIEVE THESE OBJECTIVES THROUGH VARIOUS ACTIVITIES, INCLUDING BUT NOT LIMITED TO, UPDATING VFC AND 317 VACCINE GUIDELINES IN ACCORDANCE WITH CDC POLICIES, COMPLETING NECESSARY UPDATES AND REPORTS ON VACCINE INVENTORY AND PROGRAM OPERATIONS, EDUCATING PROVIDERS, THE GENERAL PUBLIC AND HEALTHCARE PROFESSIONALS, TARGETING AT-RISK GROUPS AND DEVELOPING PROGRAMS TO IMPROVE CURRENT RATES, PERFORMING ANNUAL SURVEYS AND SURVEILLANCE OF IMMUNIZATION COVERAGE LEVELS AND VACCINE PREVENTABLE DISEASES IN THE STATE, WORKING WITH PARTNERS TO IDENTIFY PREGNANT WOMEN WITH HEPATITIS B IN ORDER TO PREVENT TRANSMISSION, ENHANCING GRITS AS NEEDED TO INCREASE USE AND PROMOTE PROGRAM GOALS, AND IMPROVING UPON PREPAREDNESS PLANS TO ASSURE STATE PREPAREDNESS FOR PANDEMICS AND OTHER EVENTS REQUIRING VACCINE RESPONSE.

top_20_records_by_obligation.transaction_description: CDC-RFA-IP19-1901 IMMUNIZATION AND VACCINES FOR CHILDREN - PROJECT ABSTRACT SUMMARY ARIZONA IMMUNIZATION PROGRAM APRIL 2019  THE ARIZONA IMMUNIZATION PROGRAM OFFICE (AIPO) WILL WORK TO FULFILL ALL REQUIREMENTS OF THE CDC-RFA-IP19-1901 TO PROVIDE IMMUNIZATION ACTIVITIES FOR UNINSURED AND UNDERINSURED INDIVIDUALS IN ARIZONA.  ADDITIONALLY, AIPO WILL WORK WITH OTHER PROGRAMS IN OUR AGENCY AND IN OUR STATE TO ENSURE THAT ARIZONA IS ABLE TO RESPOND TO ANY VACCINE PREVENTABLE DISEASE OUTBREAK IN OUR STATE.  THE AIPO WILL FOLLOW PROGRAM GUIDANCE PROVIDED IN THE IPOM AND THE NOFO.  PROGRAM COMPLIANCE FOR OUR PROGRAM AND FOR OUR PROVIDERS WILL HAVE A SIGNIFICANT FOCUS IN THIS 5 YEAR GRANT CYCLE.  THE ACTIVITIES FOR CHAPTERS REGARDING PROGRAM MANAGEMENT AND SUSTAINABILITY, PROGRAM EFFECTIVENESS, VACCINE ACCESS AND MANAGEMENT WILL ALLOW US TO ENSURE THAT VACCINES ARE AVAILABLE AND SAFE FOR ALL PARTICIPANTS IN THE IMMUNIZATION PROGRAMS.  AT THE SAME TIME AIPO WILL BE LOOKING TO IMPROVE DATA QUALITY IN OUR REGISTRY (ASIIS).  THE ACTIVITIES FOR CHAPTERS REGARDING IIS AND PROVIDER QUALITY IMPROVEMENT WILL HELP US TO REVIEW VACCINE COVERAGE LEVELS IN ARIZONA AS THE DATA IN ASIIS WILL BE MORE COMPLETE AND ACCURATE.  ADDITIONALLY, AIPO HAS WORKED HARD TO CULTIVATE AND MAINTAIN RELATIONSHIPS WITH COMMUNITIES AND INDIVIDUALS INTERESTED IN GROWING VACCINATION COVERAGE LEVELS AND REDUCING THE RISK OF VACCINE PREVENTABLE DISEASE IN ARIZONA.  THE ACTIVITIES RELATED TO THE CHAPTERS ON COMMUNICATION, PARTNERSHIP AND EDUCATION, SURVEILLANCE AND OUTBREAK RESPONSE, PERINATAL HEP B PREVENTION, PAN FLU PREPAREDNESS, SCHOOL VACCINATION COVERAGE, ADOLESCENT IMMUNIZATION AND ADULT IMMUNIZATION ALL WILL LEAD TO BETTER IMMUNIZATION COVERAGE IN ARIZONA.  VACCINATION COVERAGE LEVELS HAVE CONTINUED TO DROP IN ARIZONA SCHOOL AGED CHILDREN.  AT THE SAME TIME FEWER ELIGIBLE CHILDREN ARE BEING VACCINATED WITH THE VFC PROGRAM.  THIS COMES FROM UNREALIZED FEARS OF PENALTY FOR PROGRAM PARTICIPATION.  THE AIPO WILL CONTINUE TO WORK TO COMBAT THESE FEARS AND GET MORE CHILDREN, ADOLESCENTS AND ADULTS VACCINATED AND THEREBY REDUCE THE RISK OF THE SPREAD OF VACCINE PREVENTABLE DISEASES IN ARIZONA.  ABSTRACT SUMMARY: PROJECT BB1 VPD OUTBREAK RESPONSE RECENT OUTBREAKS OF VACCINE PREVENTABLE DISEASES (VPDS) IN ARIZONA HAVE HIGHLIGHTED THE IMPORTANCE OF STATEWIDE CAPACITY AND PARTNERSHIP BUILDING IN THE PUBLIC AND PRIVATE SECTOR. SINCE MID-2018, THERE HAS BEEN AN ONGOING OUTBREAK OF HEPATITIS A AMONG 145 INDIVIDUALS THAT HAVE RISK FACTORS OF EXPERIENCING HOMELESSNESS AND/OR DRUG USE IN PIMA AND MARICOPA COUNTIES. MORE RECENTLY, THE INFLUX OF BORDER CROSSERS HAS INCREASED INSTANCES OF MUMPS AND VARICELLA INTRODUCTIONS INTO CONGREGATE SETTINGS OF MIGRANTS, INCLUDING DETENTION CENTERS AND SHELTERS. STATEWIDE CAPACITY AND PARTNERSHIPS FOR A MORE ROBUST PUBLIC HEALTH RESPONSE ARE A CRITICAL NEED THAT THE FOLLOWING STRATEGIES AND ACTIVITIES ADDRESS. ARIZONA DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH SERVICES (ADHS) WILL DEVELOP CAPACITY TO ADDRESS VPD OUTBREAKS THROUGH TRAININGS, PROTOCOLS, AND PARTNERSHIPS. ADHS WILL PARTNER WITH THE ARIZONA PARTNERSHIP FOR IMMUNIZATION (TAPI), NON-PROFIT STATEWIDE COALITION, TO STRENGTHEN VPD RESPONSE THROUGH COLLABORATION. TAPI HAS BEEN OPERATING AS A LEADING PUBLIC/PRIVATE PARTNERSHIP FOR OVER 27 YEARS AS A NATIONAL EXAMPLE OF BEST PRACTICES IN IMMUNIZATION EDUCATION FOR ROUTINE VACCINATION. TAPI’S SYSTEMS APPROACH TO IMMUNIZATION ISSUES ASSURES BUY-IN AND ENSURES THAT EVERYONE IS CONSISTENT IN APPROACHES. THESE PROJECTS WILL BETTER PREPARE ARIZONA’S HEALTHCARE SYSTEM FOR A COORDINATED RESPONSE TO VPD OUTBREAKS. THE PROPOSED PERIOD OF PERFORMANCE IS THE FIRST BUDGET PERIOD. THE EXPECTED OUTCOMES TO BE ACHIEVED IN THE BUDGET PERIOD ARE: - IMPROVED IMPLEMENTATION OF STATEWIDE IMMUNIZATION ACTIVITIES O MEASURE: NUMBER OF PARTNERS TRAINED ON IMPLEMENTING A VACCINE RESPONSE (TAPI) - IMPROVED READINESS TO RESPOND TO VPD OUTBREAKS O MEASURE: AFTER-ACTION REPORT FROM TABLETOP EXERCISE THAT IDENTIFIES AREAS FOR IMPROVEMENT - REDUCED INC

top_20_records_by_obligation.transaction_description: CDC-RFA-IP19-1901 IMMUNIZATION AND VACCINES FOR CHILDREN - THE MICHIGAN IMMUNIZATION PROGRAM IS DIRECTLY RESPONSIBLE FOR DECREASING THE INCIDENCE OF VACCINE PREVENTABLE DISEASE, INCREASING IMMUNIZATION OPPORTUNITIES FOR MICHIGAN CITIZENS, AND EXECUTING THE FEDERAL VACCINES FOR CHILDREN (VFC) PROGRAM.  THE PURPOSE OF THIS GRANT IS TO SUPPORT EFFORTS TO PLAN, DEVELOP, AND MAINTAIN A MICHIGAN PUBLIC HEALTH INFRASTRUCTURE THAT ENSURES THE STATE ACHIEVES SUCCESS IN THIS RESPONSIBILITY. THE VFC PROGRAM INCREASES ACCESS TO VACCINES FOR ELIGIBLE CHILDREN BY SUPPLYING FEDERALLY-PURCHASED PEDIATRIC AND ADOLESCENT VACCINES TO PUBLIC AND PRIVATE HEALTH CARE PROVIDERS ENROLLED IN THE PROGRAM.  DISCRETIONARY PUBLIC HEALTH SECTION 317 FUNDS ALSO ASSIST THE STATE IN PROVIDING VACCINE TO ELIGIBLE HIGH RISK CHILDREN AND ADULTS. MICHIGAN IS ALSO APPLYING FOR COMPONENT GRANTS AA1, BB1, CC3, AND CC4.

top_20_records_by_obligation.transaction_description: CDC-RFA-IP19-1901 IMMUNIZATION AND VACCINES FOR CHILDREN - THE AIM OF THIS OHIO DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH (ODH) PROPOSAL IS TO PREVENT VACCINE-PREVENTABLE DISEASES WITHIN OHIO THROUGH MAINTAINING AN IMMUNIZATION DELIVERY INFRASTRUCTURE, AND TO PERFORM SURVEILLANCE TO DETECT, INVESTIGATE, AND CONTROL VACCINE-PREVENTABLE DISEASE OUTBREAKS. ODH WILL EMPLOY THE FOLLOWING STRATEGIES TO IMPROVE AND SUSTAIN HIGH IMMUNIZATION COVERAGE, REDUCE VACCINATION DISPARITIES AND INCIDENTS OF VACCINE PREVENTABLE DISEASES (VPD), AND IMPROVE READINESS TO RESPOND TO VPD THREATS:  1. PROGRAM MANAGEMENT AND SUSTAINABILITY   - ENSURE INFRASTRUCTURE TO SUPPORT CAPACITY, OPERATIONS, AND ACCOUNTABILITY  2. PROGRAM EFFECTIVENESS   - IDENTIFY AREAS WITH LOW VACCINATION COVERAGE   - PERFORM ACTIVITIES TO IMPROVE COVERAGE   - INTEGRATE IIS DATA WITH NIS SURVEY  3. VACCINE ACCESS AND MANAGEMENT   - MAINTAIN ENROLLED PROVIDERS TO ADMINISTER VACCINES   - PERFORM QUALITY ASSURANCE ACTIVITIES   - ADHERE TO CDC GUIDANCE FOR VACCINE FUNDING   - USE CDC MECHANISMS FOR VACCINE PLANNING, ORDERING, AND DISTRIBUTION   - ENSURE VACCINE STORAGE AND HANDLING TO MAINTAIN VIABILITY  4. IMMUNIZATION INFORMATION SYSTEMS   - ENHANCE OHIO’S IMMUNIZATION REGISTRY (IMPACTSIIS) CAPABILITIES  5. COMMUNICATION, PARTNERSHIP AND EDUCATION   - ENGAGE STAKEHOLDERS TO IMPROVE VACCINATION COVERAGE   - ADDRESS CURRENT IMMUNIZATION ISSUES   - PROMOTE EDUCATION FOR PROVIDERS AND PUBLIC  6. PROVIDER QUALITY IMPROVEMENT   - IMPLEMENT QUALITY IMPROVEMENT (QI) STRATEGIES AND MONITOR IMPACT ON COVERAGE   - USE IIS DATA TO INFORM/MANAGE QI ASSESSMENT ACTIVITIES  7.VPD SURVEILLANCE AND OUTBREAK RESPONSE   - CONDUCT SURVEILLANCE TO IDENTIFY, CONTROL & PREVENT VPD   - REPORT VPD CASES AND/OR OUTBREAKS TO HEALTH OFFICIALS   - ENCOURAGE VAERS REPORTING AND MONITOR VAERS AND VACCINE SAFETY DATA  8. PERINATAL HEPATITIS B PREVENTION   - IDENTIFY HBSAG-POSITIVE PREGNANT WOMEN AND BIRTHS   - HBV-EXPOSED NEWBORNS RECEIVE PEP   - HBV-EXPOSED INFANTS COMPETE VACCINE SERIES AND PVST  9. PANDEMIC INFLUENZA PREPAREDNESS   - COLLABORATE WITH PREPAREDNESS TO IMPLEMENT RESPONSE TO INFLUENZA PANDEMIC  10. SCHOOL VACCINATION COVERAGE   - ASSESS STUDENTS COMPLIANCE WITH VACCINATION REQUIREMENTS   - COMMUNICATE SCHOOL VACCINATION COVERAGE AND EXEMPTION ESTIMATES TO STAKEHOLDERS  11. ADOLESCENT IMMUNIZATION   - WORK WITH PARTNERS TO INCREASE COVERAGE FOR ADOLESCENTS  12. ADULT IMMUNIZATION   - WORK WITH PARTNERS TO INCREASE COVERAGE FOR ADULTS

top_20_records_by_obligation.transaction_description: JUNE 2023 SUPPLEMENTAL FUNDING PROGRAMS: HHS BRIDGE ACCESS AND VACCINE CONFIDENCE - THE VISION OF THE TEXAS DEPARTMENT OF STATE HEALTH SERVICES (DSHS) IMMUNIZATION PROGRAM (PROGRAM) IS A TEXAS FREE OF VACCINE-PREVENTABLE DISEASES. THE MISSION OF THE TEXAS DSHS IMMUNIZATION PROGRAM IS TO REMOVE BARRIERS TO COMPLETE AND TIMELY VACCINATION, INCREASE VACCINE COVERAGE LEVELS, AND REDUCE THE BURDEN OF VACCINE-PREVENTABLE DISEASES FOR ALL TEXAS INFANTS, CHILDREN, ADOLESCENTS, AND ADULTS. THE PROGRAM SEEKS TO PREVENT, REDUCE AND ULTIMATELY ELIMINATE VACCINE-PREVENTABLE DISEASES WITH AN EMPHASIS ON IMPROVING IMMUNIZATION COVERAGE AMONG OUR YOUNGEST CITIZENS, CHILDREN UNDER THREE YEARS OF AGE. MAJOR ACTIVITIES ARE ORGANIZED AROUND ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS, SUCH AS ASSESSING IMMUNIZATION COVERAGE; DISEASE SURVEILLANCE AND OUTBREAK RESPONSE; EDUCATING HEALTHCARE PROFESSIONALS; PROVIDING NEEDED INFORMATION TO PARENTS, SCHOOLS AND THE PUBLIC; REDUCING BARRIERS TO VACCINE ACCESS THROUGH THE TEXAS VACCINES FOR CHILDREN PROGRAM; ASSURING ADEQUATE VACCINE SUPPLY; MONITORING AND SUPPORTING PROVIDERS TO ENSURE PROPER VACCINE HANDLING AND ACCOUNTING; AND OPERATING IMMTRAC2, THE STATEWIDE IMMUNIZATION REGISTRY. THE PROGRAM ALSO SEEKS TO PROMOTE ADOLESCENT AND ADULT VACCINATIONS. ADOLESCENT IMMUNIZATION RATES ON HPV, TDAP, AND MCV ARE COMMUNICATED TO SITES ENROLLED IN THE TVFC PROGRAM DURING SITE REVIEWS. EDUCATION ON ACTIVITIES TO INCORPORATE AT THE SITE TO RAISE ADOLESCENT RATES, SUCH AS REMINDER/RECALL AND SIMULTANEOUS ADMINISTRATION IS PROVIDED TO STAFF DURING THE REVIEW. IN ADDITION, DSHS COMMUNICATES THE TDAP/HPV RATIO (1TDAP:2HPV) TO ALL ENROLLED SITES TWICE ANNUALLY. THIS COMMUNICATION CONTAINS INFORMATION ON ACTIVITIES TO INCORPORATE TO RAISE ADOLESCENT RATES.  THE PROGRAM EDUCATES PROVIDERS ON THE ACIP REQUIREMENTS AND IMMUNIZATIONS STANDARDS FOR ADOLESCENTS AND ADULTS. IN ADDITION, DSHS OPERATES AN ADULT SAFETY NET (ASN) PROGRAM THAT OFFERS MOST ACIP-RECOMMENDED VACCINES TO UNINSURED ADULTS IN FEDERALLY QUALIFIED HEALTH CENTERS, RURAL HEALTH CLINICS, DSHS AND LOCAL HEALTH DEPARTMENT CLINICS. IN ADDITION, OTHER SITES THAT PARTICIPATE IN THE ASN PROGRAM INCLUDE HIV/STD CLINICS AND DRUG TREATMENT FACILITIES. ANNUALLY, DSHS STAFF CONDUCT A SITE REVIEW AT FACILITIES THAT ARE ENROLLED ONLY IN ASN TO REVIEW STORAGE AND HANDLING PRACTICES, ELIGIBILITY PRACTICES AND ALL OTHER POLICIES AND PROCEDURES REQUIRED OF THE PROGRAM. IMMUNIZATION SERVICE DELIVERY IN TEXAS IS COMPLICATED BY A NUMBER OF FACTORS. TEXAS SHARES A LARGE INTERNATIONAL BORDER WITH MEXICO, AND MANY HEALTH PROBLEMS FACED BY MEXICO MUST BE ADDRESSED IN THE ADJACENT AREAS. THE PROGRAM MUST MEET THE NEEDS OF BOTH LARGE, URBAN CENTERS AND SPARSELY-POPULATED RURAL AREAS. THE DIVISION OF TEXAS INTO 254 COUNTIES UNDER LOCAL JURISDICTION MAKES STANDARDIZATION DIFFICULT. NO SINGLE INTERVENTION STRATEGY ALONE IS SUCCESSFUL IN INCREASING IMMUNIZATION COVERAGE LEVELS. A COMBINATION OF BEST PRACTICES, IMPLEMENTED CONSISTENTLY, CAN HELP TO RAISE IMMUNIZATION LEVELS. THE PROGRAM HAS IDENTIFIED AND PROMOTES THE FOLLOWING BEST PRACTICES: REMINDER AND RECALL SYSTEMS, THE MEDICAL HOME, REGISTRIES AND ROBUST EDUCATION FOR BOTH PROVIDERS AND THE PUBLIC. PARTNERSHIPS ARE AN IMPORTANT TOOL IN PUTTING THESE BEST PRACTICES INTO ACTION.  RAISING IMMUNIZATION LEVELS IS A COLLABORATIVE EFFORT THAT BENEFITS FROM THE COMMITMENT OF OTHER PROGRAMS AND AGENCIES SUCH AS TEXAS HEALTH AND HUMAN SERVICES; AND THE TEXAS EDUCATION AGENCY, AS WELL AS PRIVATE SECTOR PARTNERS SUCH AS THE TEXAS MEDICAL ASSOCIATION, TEXAS PEDIATRIC SOCIETY, AND THE TEXAS PHARMACY ASSOCIATION. THE PROGRAM WILL CONTINUE TO WORK WITH PARTNERS TO REACH OUT TO THEIR CONSTITUENCIES AND ENHANCE THEIR IMMUNIZATION EFFORTS. FUNDING OF THIS APPLICATION WILL MAKE IT POSSIBLE FOR THE PROGRAM TO CONTINUE SUPPORT OF IMMUNIZATION ACTIVITIES ON A STATEWIDE BASIS.
